definition_zh: 易受攻击的；脆弱的；易受伤的；易受影响的
definition_en: easily harmed, attacked or affected, because of weakness or lack of protection
core_image: 一层铠甲上有一道没盖住的缝，箭正好能扎进去
scene: 夜里山路没有护栏，老人拄着棍慢慢走，一点风都能让人打晃。Young plants are vulnerable to frost in late spring.
sceneCN: 这里 vulnerable 是「易受伤害的」（第 1 个义项：因脆弱或缺乏保护而容易受损）；句意为幼苗容易受晚春霜冻伤害。铠甲上留着缝的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 脆弱的；易受攻击的；易受影响的

derivatives.zh: 脆弱性；易受攻击之处
脆弱地；无保护地
不会受伤的；刀枪不入的
（旧）伤药

senses.title: Easy to be hurt physically
senses.definition: easily injured because of thin skin, weak health or lack of shelter
senses.definitionCN: 因皮薄、体弱或无所庇护而容易受伤
senses.example: Young plants are vulnerable to frost in late spring.
senses.exampleCN: 幼苗容易受到晚春霜冻的伤害。
senses.why: The Latin word meant wounding, so the adjective began with the body and what can cut it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词意为「致伤」，所以这个形容词从身体和能划伤身体的东西开始。

senses.title: Open to attack or criticism
senses.titleCN: 易受攻击的；易受指责的
senses.definition: weak in a way that an enemy or a critic can use
senses.definitionCN: 弱点明显，能被对手或批评者利用
senses.example: The old bridge is vulnerable to a single well-aimed charge.
senses.exampleCN: 这座旧桥经不起一次准确地放置的爆破。
senses.why: A wound is not only physical, so a wall with a weak point is said to be vulnerable in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 伤口不只在身上，所以有弱点的城墙也用同一个词形容。

senses.title: Needing social protection
senses.definition: used of people or groups who need help, such as the elderly, the poor or the sick
senses.definitionCN: 形容需要帮助的人或群体，如老人、穷人、病人
senses.example: Social workers visit the most vulnerable families each week.
senses.exampleCN: 社工每周探访最脆弱的那些家庭。
senses.why: In policy writing the wounded side is a group left without cover, and the word turns into a term of care.
senses.whyCN: 在政策文本里，「会被伤到的一方」就是无处遮蔽的人群，这个词便成了照料用语。

senses.title: Easily affected by something
senses.definition: likely to be affected badly by a disease, a market or a change
senses.definitionCN: 容易因病、市场或变化而受害
senses.example: Farms here are vulnerable to a fall in the price of grain.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的农场容易受粮价下跌的打击。
senses.why: Anything that can be hurt by a change of condition gets the same adjective, whether a body or a business.
senses.whyCN: 凡会因条件变化而受损的东西都得到同一个形容词，身体也罢，生意也罢。

senses.title: Defenceless in feeling
senses.titleCN: （情感上）容易受伤的；毫无防备
senses.definition: feeling exposed and easily hurt, in emotional use
senses.definitionCN: 情感层面指暴露、易被伤害
senses.example: After the move he felt vulnerable among strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 搬来以后，他在陌生人中间感到没有依靠。
senses.why: With no armour of habit or friends, the feeling is the bodily one carried inward.
senses.whyCN: 没有习惯与朋友作护甲，这种感觉就是把身体上的那层搬进了心里。

intro.en: Vulnerable comes from Latin vulnerare, to wound, from vulnus, a wound.
intro.cn: vulnerable 来自拉丁语 vulnerare（使受伤），源出 vulnus（伤口）。

items.en: Vulnus meant a wound, and vulnerare meant to inflict one.
items.cn: vulnus 意为伤口，vulnerare 意为使受伤。

items.en: Vulnerabilis described a spot that could be wounded, said of bodies and of walls.
items.cn: vulnerabilis 形容能被伤到的位置，身体与城墙都可用。

items.en: Military writers used it for the one open part of a fortification, and the military sense survives.
items.cn: 军事作家用它指防御工事里未被掩护的那一块，这一层含义延续至今。

items.en: English took the word in the seventeenth century for what can be hurt.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪引入这个词，指能被伤到的东西。

items.en: Modern policy language extended it to people and economies that need protection.
items.cn: 现代政策语言把它扩展到需要保护的人群与经济体。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the Latin root for a wound, the second the adjectives of weakness nearby.
note.cn: 第一组收建立在拉丁「伤口」词根上的词，第二组收近处表示脆弱的形容词。

entries.definition: The state of being open to harm.
entries.definitionCN: 脆弱性；易受攻击之处

entries.definition: The adverb, in an exposed way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，无保护地

entries.definition: Unable to be wounded at all.
entries.definitionCN: 不会受伤的

entries.definition: The Latin noun for a wound.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语「伤口」

entries.definition: Easily broken, of objects and health.
entries.definitionCN: 易碎的；脆弱的

entries.definition: Left without cover or shelter.
entries.definitionCN: 暴露的；无遮蔽的

entries.definition: Lacking strength, the plainest word of the set.
entries.definitionCN: 弱的，最朴素的词

entries.definition: Unable to be beaten, the confident opposite.
entries.definitionCN: 不可战胜的

normalIntro.en: The root is the wound, so everything called vulnerable has somewhere a wound can get in.
normalIntro.cn: 词根是「伤口」，凡被称为 vulnerable 的东西，都有个地方能让伤钻进去。

normal.en: Vulnus is a wound, so vulnerable means woundable.
normal.cn: vulnus 是伤口，vulnerable 就是能被伤到的。

normal.en: The noun ends in -ability: vulnerability.
normal.cn: 名词以 -ability 结尾：vulnerability。

normal.en: In- makes it safe: invulnerable.
normal.cn: 加 in- 就安全了：invulnerable。

normal.en: Vulnerable to, never vulnerable of.
normal.cn: 搭配是 vulnerable to，不是 vulnerable of。

normal.en: Old armour and young plants share the same word.
normal.cn: 旧铠甲与幼苗用的是同一个词。

abstract.en: See a gap in a metal coat where an arrow can land.
abstract.cn: 想铁衣上一道缝，箭正能落进去。

abstract.en: Hear wind against a house with no shutters.
abstract.cn: 听风吹一栋没有窗板的房子。

abstract.en: Feel a newcomer standing alone at a party door.
abstract.cn: 感受新来的人独自站在聚会门口。

examples.en: The coast is vulnerable to storms in winter.
examples.cn: 这段海岸冬季容易受风暴侵袭。

examples.en: Old people are more vulnerable to the cold.
examples.cn: 老人更容易受寒。

examples.en: The system is vulnerable because one password protects everything.
examples.cn: 一个密码保护所有东西，这个系统因此很脆弱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外了呢」——外头的护甲被卸下来了，人就没了遮挡。

root: 拉丁语 vulnus（伤口）→ vulnerare（使受伤）→ vulnerabilis（可被伤到的）→ 英语 vulnerable。

sensesIntro.en: A word about wounds moves from the body, to walls, to social groups, to markets and to feelings.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个关于伤口的词，从身体走到城墙，再到人群、市场与情感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gap in the armour.
core.cn: 核心意象：铠甲上的一处缝。

branches.en: The body branch: seedlings in late frost.
branches.cn: 身体分支：晚霜里的幼苗。

branches.en: The defence branch: an old bridge, one charge.
branches.cn: 防御分支：一座旧桥与一次爆破。

branches.en: The social branch: the most vulnerable families.
branches.cn: 社会分支：最脆弱的家庭。

branches.en: The market branch: grain prices that swing.
branches.cn: 市场分支：摇摆的粮价。

branches.en: The feeling branch: a stranger among strangers.
branches.cn: 情感分支：陌生人中的陌生人。

intro.en: Vulner- is the wound; -able makes it possible, -ability makes the quality and in- removes it.
intro.cn: vulner- 是伤口，-able 表示可能，-ability 表示性质，in- 则表示取消。

latinIntro.en: Latin vulnus, vulnerare and vulnerabilis are recorded, and the wounding root appears in no other English base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vulnus、vulnerare、vulnerabilis 均有文献，这个「致伤」词根在英语里没有别的基底。

items.example: It is the only base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词族唯一的基底。

items.example: It is the seed of the family.
It forms vulneraries, old wound herbs.

definition_zh: 工资；报酬；发动（战争）；进行（斗争）
definition_en: money paid to a worker for work done, usually hourly or daily, or to carry on a war or a campaign
core_image: 一周的工时记在纸上，换成一叠按周发的钱
scene: 工厂门口的告示牌上写着新的时薪，工人们围着看了很久。The workers asked for a higher wage and shorter hours.
sceneCN: 这里 wage 是「工资」（第 1 个义项：按工计酬的钱，常按周或按小时发）；句意为工人们要求提高工资、缩短工时。那块写着时薪的告示牌，就是这个词的日常画面。

pos.zh: 发动（战争）；进行（斗争）；开展（运动）

derivatives.zh: 复数形式，常指一笔工资，也指「报应、代价」
同形近词，义为「赌注；打赌」，来源不同
复合词，义为「挣工资的人；工薪族」

senses.title: Money paid for work
senses.definition: money paid regularly to a worker, usually for hours or days worked
senses.definitionCN: 按工时或工日定期付给工人的钱
senses.example: The workers asked for a higher wage and shorter hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们要求提高工资、缩短工时。
senses.why: The word began as a promise to pay, from a Germanic root for a pledge; a wage is money promised for work.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指「许诺付给的报酬」，源自日耳曼语表示「抵押、许诺」的词根，所以 wage 就是为工作许诺付的钱。

senses.title: The plural as a sum or a price
senses.definition: the plural wages for the money as a whole, or for what a deed finally costs
senses.definitionCN: 复数 wages 指整笔工资，也指某行为的最终代价
senses.example: The wages of that carelessness were heavy.
senses.exampleCN: 那次疏忽的代价很沉重。
senses.why: A sum of money owed for work became a general image of what any action finally pays out.
senses.whyCN: 为工作应付的一笔钱，进而成了任何行为最终「付出的钱」的普遍比喻。

senses.title: To carry on a war
senses.definition: to begin and continue a war or a long struggle
senses.definitionCN: 开始并持续进行战争或长期斗争
senses.example: The two states waged war for nearly a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 两国交战将近十年。
senses.why: The old verb meant to pledge oneself to a fight; to wage war is to put that pledge into action.
senses.whyCN: 旧时动词义为「以自己为质投入战斗」，wage war 就是把这份许诺付诸行动。

senses.title: To carry on a campaign
senses.definition: to conduct a long public effort, as a campaign against disease
senses.definitionCN: 长期进行某种公众努力，如对抗疾病的运动
senses.example: The town waged a long campaign for clean water.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇为清洁水源开展了长期运动。
senses.why: From war the verb widened to any sustained struggle that must be carried on over time.
senses.whyCN: 从战争出发，动词扩展到任何需要长期坚持的斗争。

senses.title: To bet or stake
senses.definition: in older use, to stake money on a result
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法中，拿钱赌一个结果
senses.example: He wagered his whole month's pay on one race.
senses.exampleCN: 他把整月的工钱全押在一场比赛上。
senses.why: The staking sense came through wager from the same root of pledge; here a promise is put at risk.
senses.whyCN: 下注义经 wager 从同一「抵押、许诺」词根而来，此时许诺被置于风险之中。

intro.en: Wage comes from a Germanic root meaning a pledge or a stake, borrowed through Old French.
intro.cn: wage 来自日耳曼语表示「抵押、许质」的词根，经古法语借入英语。

items.en: The root behind wage meant a pledge or a sum put up as security.
items.cn: wage 背后的词根意为抵押或许诺的保证金。

items.en: Old French wage and gage carried the idea of a pledge into France.
items.cn: 古法语 wage 与 gage 把「抵押」的观念带进法国。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the middle ages as a payment promised for service.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪借入该词，指为服役许诺的报酬。

items.en: A verb to wage battle grew beside it, meaning to put oneself up as pledge for a fight.
items.cn: 旁边长出动词 wage battle，意为以自身作质投入战斗。

items.en: Modern use split the pair: wage as regular pay, and wage a war or a campaign.
items.cn: 现代用法分作两支：wage 作定期工资，以及 wage a war 或 wage a campaign。

note.en: The first group holds the words that look or sound close, the second the words for pay and pay-related actions.
note.cn: 第一组收形近音近词，第二组收与报酬及开战相关的词。

entries.definition: The plural, often meaning pay as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 复数，常指整笔工资。

entries.definition: A bet, from the same pledge root but a different path.
entries.definitionCN: 赌注，同出「抵押」词根但路径不同。

entries.definition: The past tense of the verb, as in waged a campaign.
entries.definitionCN: 动词过去式，如 waged a campaign。

entries.definition: To move a tail from side to side; unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 摇尾巴，与此词无关。

entries.definition: Pay stated as a yearly sum, usually monthly.
entries.definitionCN: 按年额计、通常按月发的报酬。

entries.definition: The everyday word covering all kinds of payment.
entries.definitionCN: 各类报酬的日常统称。

entries.definition: All money coming in, from work and other sources.
entries.definitionCN: 收入，包括劳动与其他来源。

entries.definition: Money gained by work, often over a period.
entries.definitionCN: 劳动所得，常按一段时间计。

normalIntro.en: A pledge gives both a salary and a war: what is promised for work, and what is staked in a fight.
normalIntro.cn: 「许诺」同时生出工资与战争：为工作许诺的报酬，为战斗押上的本身。

normal.en: Wage is pay for hours or days; salary is a yearly figure paid monthly.
normal.cn: wage 按小时或工日计，salary 按年额按月发。

normal.en: The plural wages means the pay as a whole, not many salaries.
normal.cn: 复数 wages 指整笔工资，不是很多份工资。

normal.en: Wage a war, wage a campaign: the verb needs a struggle after it.
normal.cn: wage a war、wage a campaign：这个动词后面要接斗争。

normal.en: Wag is a different word: a dog wags its tail.
normal.cn: wag 是另一个词：狗摇尾巴。

normal.en: The minimum wage is the legal floor for hourly pay.
normal.cn: the minimum wage 是时薪的法定下限。

abstract.en: See a paper slip of hours turning into cash on a Friday.
abstract.cn: 想一张工时单在周五变成现金。

abstract.en: Hear coins counted out on a wooden counter.
abstract.cn: 听硬币在木柜台上被数出来。

abstract.en: Feel a promise made before the work even began.
abstract.cn: 感受工作在开始前就已给出的许诺。

examples.en: His weekly wage barely covers the rent.
examples.cn: 他的周薪勉强够付房租。

examples.en: The union fought for a fair wage.
examples.cn: 工会为公平的工资而斗争。

examples.en: The country waged a long war over water rights.
examples.cn: 这个国家为水权打了很久的仗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「胃哥」——胃哥干活最卖力，只为月底那笔工资。

root: 日耳曼语 *wadi-（抵押、许诺）→ 古法语 wage/gage → 英语 wage（工资）；同根并生动词义「发动战争」。

sensesIntro.en: A pledge stretches in two directions: money promised for work, and oneself pledged to a struggle.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个「许诺」向两个方向伸展：为工作许诺的钱，以及把自己押上的斗争。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a paper of hours exchanged for cash.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张工时单换成一笔现金。

branches.en: The pay branch: a demand for higher hourly pay.
branches.cn: 报酬分支：要求提高时薪。

branches.en: The price branch: the wages of carelessness.
branches.cn: 代价分支：疏忽的代价。

branches.en: The war branch: two states waging war for a decade.
branches.cn: 战争分支：两国交战十年。

branches.en: The campaign branch: a town fighting for clean water.
branches.cn: 运动分支：全镇为清洁水源而奋斗。

branches.en: The stake branch: a month of pay on one race.
branches.cn: 下注分支：一个月的工钱押在一场比赛上。

intro.en: Wage has no productive prefix; the family is made of the plural -es, the past -ed and a few compounds.
intro.cn: wage 没有能产的词缀，词族由复数 -es、过去式 -ed 和少量复合词构成。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic, not Latin; it reached English through Old French, so no Latin entry is given.
latinIntro.cn: 词根为日耳曼语而非拉丁语，经古法语进入英语，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The root gives both pay and warfare.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根同时生出报酬与战争。

items.example: The spelling settled with a final e.
items.exampleCN: 拼写最终带一个不发音的 e。

items.meaning: more than one, or he does

items.exampleCN: 它构成 wager 与 wage-earner。

definition_zh: 四轮马车；货车；车皮
definition_en: a vehicle with four wheels, pulled by animals or an engine and used to carry goods
core_image: 两匹马拉着高帮的木车，轮子在土路上碾出两道深印
scene: 集市散场，帮工把菜筐一只只搬上车，车夫扯了扯缰绳，车轮吱吱地压过石板路。The wagon rolled slowly towards the river with a load of hay.
sceneCN: 这里 wagon 是「四轮马车」（第 1 个义项：由畜力或机器牵引、用于载货的四轮车）；句意为一辆装干草的马车缓缓朝河边驶去。木车在土路上留两道深印的那幅画就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 赶车人；车夫
wagon 的英式拼法
一车之量
旅行车（美式）

senses.title: A four-wheeled cart for goods
senses.definition: a strong cart with four wheels, pulled by horses or oxen and used to move goods
senses.definitionCN: 四轮的结实大车，由马或牛牵引运货
senses.example: The wagon rolled slowly towards the river with a load of hay.
senses.exampleCN: 一辆装满干草的马车缓缓朝河边驶去。
senses.why: The word came from Dutch and named the plain working cart of farm and market.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自荷兰语，指农场与集市上用的一般活计车。

senses.title: A railway truck
senses.definition: in British use, an open railway truck for goods rather than passengers
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法中指针运货而不载客的敞篷铁路车厢
senses.example: A long line of coal wagons stood waiting in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 调车场里停着一长列等着装煤的车皮。
senses.why: Railways simply moved the old word from the road to the rail, keeping its job of carrying goods.
senses.whyCN: 铁路只是把这个旧词从土路搬到铁轨上，保留它运货的职分。

senses.title: A covered settler vehicle
senses.definition: in American history, the covered wagon that carried families westward
senses.definitionCN: 美国历史中载着家庭向西迁徙的带篷车
senses.example: Their family crossed the plains in a single wagon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一家只靠一辆篷车横穿草原。
senses.why: The same cart, given a canvas cover, became both house and transport for settlers.
senses.whyCN: 同一辆大车加上帆布篷，就成了移民的住所兼交通工具。

senses.title: Part of a compound name
senses.definition: in compound names, a vehicle built on the same frame, as in station wagon or chuck wagon
senses.definitionCN: 复合名称中指同底盘的车型，如旅行车与流动餐车
senses.example: He parked the station wagon outside the diner.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旅行车停在餐车小馆外面。
senses.why: The carrying body of the old cart survives in names of vehicles built to hold things.
senses.whyCN: 旧大车的载货身形，存活在那些为装东西而造的车辆名称里。

senses.title: A figure for giving up
senses.definition: in the phrase fall off the wagon, to return to a bad habit such as drinking
senses.definitionCN: 在 fall off the wagon 中，指重新染上酗酒等恶习
senses.example: He stayed dry for a year and then fell off the wagon.
senses.exampleCN: 他戒了一年，后来又喝上了。
senses.why: The phrase came from temperance speech, where staying on the water wagon meant drinking no alcohol.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法出自戒酒宣传：待在运水车上，就是不喝酒。

intro.en: Wagon came into English from Dutch wagen, a word for a farm cart, in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: wagon 在十六世纪从荷兰语 wagen（农用大车）进入英语。

items.en: Wagen meant a wagon or cart, and Dutch trade and farming brought the word to England.
items.cn: wagen 意为大车，荷兰的贸易与农事把这个词带到了英格兰。

items.en: The Dutch word descends from a Germanic root for a vehicle, related to English way and to wain.
items.cn: 这个荷兰词源自日耳曼语表示车辆的词根，与英语 way、wain 有关。

items.en: English spelt it waggon for centuries, and wagon was later fixed in American use.
items.cn: 英语曾长期拼作 waggon，后来美式用法定下 wagon。

items.en: Railways gave the word a new job for goods trucks, still common in British speech.
items.cn: 铁路给它添了运货车皮的新用法，这一层在英式英语里仍然常见。

items.en: In America the covered wagon became a national image, and the station wagon followed the car.
items.cn: 在美洲，带篷车成了国民意象，汽车时代又有旅行车接续。

note.en: The first group gathers the cart family and spellings, the second the other vehicles of the road and rail.
note.cn: 第一组收大车词族与不同拼法，第二组收路上与铁道上其他的车。

entries.definition: The plural form.
entries.definitionCN: 复数形式

entries.definition: The older British spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的英式拼法

entries.definition: The person who drives a wagon.
entries.definitionCN: 赶车人

entries.definition: The road the wagon travels, from the same old root.
entries.definitionCN: 路，与 wagon 同源

entries.definition: A cart usually has only two wheels.
entries.definitionCN: 通常只有两轮的推车

entries.definition: A wheeled vehicle, often for passengers.
entries.definitionCN: 客车；马车

entries.definition: A motor goods vehicle, the modern heir of the wagon.
entries.definitionCN: 卡车

entries.definition: The British word for a large motor truck.
entries.definitionCN: 英式的大卡车

normalIntro.en: Wagon is a borrowed working word, so it is best held by the picture of four wheels and a load.
normalIntro.cn: wagon 是个借来的干活用的词，最好靠「四个轮子加一车货」的画面记住。

normal.en: Four wheels and a load is the whole idea of a wagon.
normal.cn: 四个轮子加一车货，就是 wagon 的全部意思。

normal.en: Wagons carry goods; carriages carry people.
normal.cn: wagon 运货，carriage 载人。

normal.en: British spelling waggon has a double g.
normal.cn: 英式拼法 waggon 是两个 g。

normal.en: A station wagon is the car version, still a carrier.
normal.cn: 旅行车是汽车版本，仍然在载东西。

normal.en: Off the wagon means drinking again, as if stepping off a cart.
normal.cn: off the wagon 指又喝上了，仿佛从车上下来。

abstract.en: See two deep ruts in a wet lane.
abstract.cn: 想湿泥路上两道深辙。

abstract.en: Hear a wooden wheel creak over stone.
abstract.cn: 听木轮在石板上吱吱作响。

abstract.en: Feel a heavy load settle and the cart push forward.
abstract.cn: 感受重货落稳，车往前一推。

examples.en: They loaded the wagon with apples before dawn.
examples.cn: 天亮前他们把苹果装上了马车。

examples.en: A line of wagons waited outside the mill.
examples.cn: 一列车等在磨坊外。

examples.en: The children rode in the back of the wagon.
examples.cn: 孩子们坐在马车后斗里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挖根」——车轮太重，把路上的土挖出了两道深根似的辙。

root: 荷兰语 wagen（大车）→ 英语 wagon；更早源自日耳曼语表示车辆的词根，与 way、wain 同源。

sensesIntro.en: One working cart spreads into the railway truck, the settler’s covered wagon, the modern estate car and one old drinker’s idiom.
sensesIntro.cn: 一辆干活的大车，扩展成铁路车皮、移民的篷车、现代的旅行车，以及一句老酒鬼的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: four wooden wheels under a load.
core.cn: 核心意象：一车货下的四个木轮。

branches.en: The farm branch: hay going down to the river.
branches.cn: 农事分支：干草车往河边走。

branches.en: The railway branch: coal trucks in the yard.
branches.cn: 铁路分支：调车场里的煤车。

branches.en: The settler branch: one wagon across the plains.
branches.cn: 移民分支：一辆车横穿草原。

branches.en: The car branch: the estate car outside a diner.
branches.cn: 汽车分支：小馆外的旅行车。

branches.en: The idiom branch: sober for a year, then not.
branches.cn: 习语分支：戒了一年，又喝了。

intro.en: Wagon is a whole borrowed word; its parts are old Germanic, and the family grows with -er and the spelling waggon.
intro.cn: wagon 是整词借入，其内部构件属古日耳曼语，词族靠 -er 与拼法 waggon 扩展。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here; the word is Germanic and came through Dutch, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语来源，属日耳曼语并经由荷兰语传入，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: The root is shared with way.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与 way 共用。

items.example: The direct source of the English word.
The Dutch ending stayed in English.
items.exampleCN: 荷兰语词尾留在了英语里。

items.example: Same old root, a different branch.

definition_zh: 腰；腰部；（衣服的）腰身；腰围
definition_en: the part of the body between the ribs and the hips, or the part of a garment that fits around it
core_image: 两手叉在身体中段，那里最窄也最能弯
scene: 裁缝绕着她的腰量了一圈，把数字写在纸样边上。The coat was taken in at the waist so that it fitted better.
sceneCN: 这里 waist 是「腰部」（第 1 个义项：肋骨与胯之间的身体部分）；句意为大衣在腰部收窄，以便更合身。两手叉腰的那处身体中段，就是这个词的形象。

derivatives.zh: waist 与 coat 复合，义为「马甲」
waist 与 band 复合，义为「腰带；裤腰」
waist 与 line 复合，义为「腰线；腰围」
加 -ed 构成，常与形容词连用，如 high-waisted「高腰的」

senses.title: The middle of the body
senses.definition: the narrow middle part of the body between the chest and the hips
senses.definitionCN: 身体在胸与胯之间较窄的中段
senses.example: The coat was taken in at the waist so that it fitted better.
senses.exampleCN: 大衣在腰部收窄，以便更合身。
senses.why: The old word meant growth, then the place where a body grows and bends; the middle of the trunk took the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的旧义是「生长」，随后指身体生长弯曲之处，躯干的中段便得了这个名字。

senses.title: The part of a garment there
senses.definition: the part of a dress, skirt or trousers that sits around the waist
senses.definitionCN: 裙、裤等衣服围绕腰部的那一部分
senses.example: The skirt has a wide waist with a hidden zip.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子腰身宽松，还藏着一个拉链。
senses.why: A garment copies the body it covers, so the middle seam of a dress is simply called the waist.
senses.whyCN: 衣服照抄它所包住的身体，裙子的中段接缝就被直接称为 waist。

senses.title: The measurement around it
senses.definition: the measurement of the body at that narrow point
senses.definitionCN: 在身体最窄处量出的周长
senses.example: His waist has not changed in twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他的腰围二十年没有变化。
senses.why: A size is quoted as the measurement of a part, so clothes are sold by waist as well as by chest.
senses.whyCN: 尺码常以某部位的测量值表示，所以衣服既按胸围也按腰围出售。

senses.title: The narrow middle of a thing
senses.definition: the narrower middle of a ship, an object or a shape
senses.definitionCN: 船体、器物或形状较窄的中段
senses.example: The ship was struck just forward of the waist.
senses.exampleCN: 船在腰段稍前处被击中。
senses.why: Any long body that swells at the ends and narrows in the middle can borrow the name of the human waist.
senses.whyCN: 任何两端粗、中间窄的长形物都可借用人腰的名字。

senses.title: The middle section of a violin family
senses.definition: the inward-curved middle of the body of a violin or a guitar
senses.definitionCN: 小提琴或吉他琴身向内收的中段
senses.example: The maker cut the waist of the instrument by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 制琴师手工把琴身的中腰挖出来。
senses.why: Instrument makers named the curved middle after the body, because the curve lets the bow move freely across the strings.
senses.whyCN: 制琴师按人体给这个弯中段命名，因为这段弯曲让弓能自由过弦。

intro.en: Waist goes back to a Germanic word for growth, which then named the growing middle of the body.
intro.cn: waist 上溯到日耳曼语表示「生长」的词，随后指身体生长、弯折的中段。

items.en: The root meant to grow, and the noun meant growth or increase.
items.cn: 词根意为生长，名词义为生长、增加。

items.en: Old English wæstm is recorded meaning growth, a fruit or a produce.
items.cn: 古英语 wæstm 有记录，义为生长、果实或收成。

items.en: The sense narrowed to the body's growing part, then to the narrow middle between ribs and hips.
items.cn: 词义缩到身体的生长部位，再缩到肋骨与胯之间的窄中段。

items.en: Tailoring took it over for the fitting part of a garment and for the size sold by it.
items.cn: 裁缝业借它指衣服合身的那一段，以及据它出售的尺码。

items.en: Shipbuilders and violin makers extended it to the narrow middle of what they make.
items.cn: 造船与制琴把它扩展到所造之物较窄的中段。

note.en: The first group follows the family and a common homophone, the second the neighbouring words for the body and for clothes.
note.cn: 第一组收同族词与常见同音词，第二组收身体与衣着的邻近词。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数。

entries.definition: A different word meaning loss or rubbish, with the same sound.
entries.definitionCN: 同音异义词，义为浪费、废物。

entries.definition: The band of cloth around the top of trousers.
entries.definitionCN: 裤子顶部的腰围布带。

entries.definition: The line of the waist, and the measurement at it.
entries.definitionCN: 腰线，以及腰围尺寸。

entries.definition: The joint beside and below the waist.
entries.definitionCN: 腰侧下方的髋部。

entries.definition: The front of the body between chest and waist.
entries.definitionCN: 胸与腰之间的腹部前面。

entries.definition: The strap worn around the waist.
entries.definitionCN: 系在腰上的带子。

entries.definition: The trunk of the body, of which the waist is the narrow part.
entries.definitionCN: 躯干，腰是其中较窄的一段。

normalIntro.en: One short word, four long compounds, and one homophone to keep apart.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短词、四个复合词，以及一个必须分开的同音词。

normal.en: Waste and waist sound alike but waste is loss, waist is the body.
normal.cn: waste 与 waist 同音，但 waste 是浪费，waist 是身体部位。

normal.en: Compounds keep the spelling: waistcoat, waistband, waistline.
normal.cn: 复合词保留拼写：waistcoat、waistband、waistline。

normal.en: A waistcoat is a garment at the waist, a vest in American use.
normal.cn: waistcoat 是穿在腰部的衣物，美式称 vest。

normal.en: Tailored clothes are taken in at the waist.
normal.cn: 定制的衣服在腰部收窄。

normal.en: A violin has a waist because its sides curve inwards.
normal.cn: 小提琴有腰身，因为两侧向内弯。

abstract.en: Picture hands on the narrowest part of the body.
abstract.cn: 想两只手叉在身体最窄处。

abstract.en: See a ribbon tied around the middle of a parcel.
abstract.cn: 想一条丝带扎在包裹的中段。

abstract.en: Feel the inward curve of a guitar against your knee.
abstract.cn: 感受吉他的内弯贴在膝上。

examples.en: She tied the apron around her waist.
examples.cn: 她把围裙系在腰上。

examples.en: The water came up to his waist.
examples.cn: 水没到他的腰部。

examples.en: This dress is loose at the waist.
examples.cn: 这条裙子腰部较松。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「围丝」——用丝带围在腰上的那圈，就是腰部。

root: 日耳曼语 *wahs-（生长）→ 古英语 wæstm（生长、果实）→ 中古英语 waist（身体中段）→ 现代英语 waist。

sensesIntro.en: Growth narrows into the middle of the body, then spreads out again into clothes, sizes, ships and violins.
sensesIntro.cn: 「生长」先缩成身体中段，再向外铺开成衣服、尺码、船体与提琴的腰。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands on the narrow middle of the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手叉在身体较窄的中段。

branches.en: The body branch: a coat taken in at the waist.
branches.cn: 身体分支：腰部收窄的大衣。

branches.en: The clothing branch: a skirt with a wide waist.
branches.cn: 衣着分支：腰身宽松的裙子。

branches.en: The size branch: a waist unchanged for twenty years.
branches.cn: 尺码分支：二十年不变的腰围。

branches.en: The object branch: the waist of a ship.
branches.cn: 器物分支：船的中腰。

branches.en: The instrument branch: the curved waist of a violin.
branches.cn: 乐器分支：小提琴内弯的中腰。

intro.en: Waist- already carries the body meaning; the compounds add coat, band, line and a past ending.
intro.cn: waist- 本身已带身体义，复合词再加 coat、band、line 与过去式词尾。

latinIntro.en: This root is Germanic; it has no Latin ancestor, so the entry lists no Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: 该词根为日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先，故不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The noun is the base of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是词族的基底。

items.example: It forms strip to the waist.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 strip to the waist。

items.example: Waste is a different word entirely.

definition_zh: 漫游；闲逛；迷路；走神；（道路、河流）蜿蜒
definition_en: to walk slowly with no fixed direction or aim, or to drift away from the subject
core_image: 一个人在陌生的小巷里左拐右转，没有目的地
scene: 下午的旧城里，游客不查地图，随便顺着石阶往上走。We wandered through the old quarter until the light began to fail.
sceneCN: 这里 wander 是「闲逛、漫游」（第 1 个义项：没有固定方向地慢慢走）；句意为我们在老城区闲逛，直到天色暗下来。顺着石阶随便走的那副样子，就是这个词的形象。

pos.zh: 漫游；闲逛；迷路；走神；（路、河）蜿蜒

collocations.phrase: a river wanders through the fields

derivatives.zh: wander 加 -er 构成，义为「漫游者；流浪者」
加 -ing 构成，义为「漫游的；流浪的」
复数形式，义为「漫游；游历见闻」
同族动词，义为「行走；往…去」，常见于 wend one's way

senses.title: To move about without a fixed course
senses.definition: to move from place to place without a planned route or a clear aim
senses.definitionCN: 无预定路线、无明确目的地地四处走动
senses.example: We wandered through the old quarter until the light began to fail.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在老城区闲逛，直到天色暗下来。
senses.why: Old English wandrian meant to move about with no fixed purpose, and the core of the word has never changed.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wandrian 指漫无目的地四处移动，这个词的核心至今未变。

senses.title: To stray from the way
senses.definition: to leave the proper path or the group, sometimes getting lost
senses.definitionCN: 离开该走的路或队伍，有时会迷路
senses.example: One child wandered off near the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 一个孩子在桥边走散了。
senses.why: Without a course, the next step is to lose the course; straying is a natural extension of aimless movement.
senses.whyCN: 没有路线，下一步便是丢了路线；走散是漫无目的移动的自然延伸。

senses.title: Of the mind, to drift
senses.definition: of thoughts, to drift from one topic to another without control
senses.definitionCN: 指思绪不受控制地从一个题目飘到另一个
senses.example: His mind began to wander as the lecture went on.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座继续时他的心思开始游移。
senses.why: Thoughts move the way feet do when no goal holds them, so the same verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 没有目标约束时，思绪移动的方式正如脚步，于是同一个动词兼指二者。

senses.title: To diverge from the point
senses.definition: to talk or write in a way that leaves the main subject
senses.definitionCN: 说话或写作时离开主要话题
senses.example: The speaker wandered from the question more than once.
senses.exampleCN: 发言者不止一次偏离了问题。
senses.why: Wandering from a road and wandering from a subject are the same picture: off the marked line.
senses.whyCN: 从路上走开与从话题上走开是同一幅图：离开了标好的线。

senses.title: Of a road or a river, to curve
senses.definition: to extend in a winding course rather than a straight line
senses.definitionCN: 以弯曲而非直线的路径延伸
senses.example: A narrow path wanders along the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 一条小径沿河岸蜿蜒。
senses.why: A road with no straight aim goes round and round, which is exactly the movement of a wanderer.
senses.whyCN: 不取直线目标的道路绕来绕去，正与漫游者的走法相同。

senses.title: A walk taken without aim
senses.definition: in informal use, a slow walk with no purpose
senses.definitionCN: 口语中指没有目的的缓慢行走
senses.example: We went for a wander along the seafront.
senses.exampleCN: 我们沿着海滨随便走了走。
senses.why: The noun simply packages the verb's aimless walk as an outing.
senses.whyCN: 名词把动词那个无目的的走法打包成一次外出。

intro.en: Wander is an Old English verb of uncertain deeper origin, already meaning to roam.
intro.cn: wander 是古英语动词，更早来源不确定，当时已表示漫游。

items.en: Wandrian meant to move about without a fixed purpose; it already had the modern sense.
items.cn: wandrian 意为无固定目的地四处移动，已具现代含义。

items.en: A related Germanic verb wanden meant to go or to wend, and gave English wend.
items.cn: 相关的日耳曼语动词 wanden 意为去、行走，生出英语 wend。

items.en: The deeper root is debated; some link it to a word for twisting, but nothing is settled.
items.cn: 更早词根有争议，有人认为与表示「扭、绕」的词有关，但无定论。

items.en: English kept the plain sense of roaming and added the mind's drifting in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语保留漫游的基本义，十六世纪又添上思绪游移之义。

items.en: Modern use adds the winding of paths and rivers and the informal noun.
items.cn: 现代用法又添上路径与河流的蜿蜒，以及口语名词。

note.en: The first group holds the words of the same root and spelling neighbours, the second the walking words it is confused with.
note.cn: 第一组收同根词与拼写相近词，第二组收容易混淆的行走类词。

entries.definition: A person who wanders; a rover.
entries.definitionCN: 漫游者、流浪者。

entries.definition: The act of roaming, or an adjective for it.
entries.definitionCN: 漫游，也可作形容词。

entries.definition: A different word meaning amazement or to ask oneself.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个词，义为惊奇、想知道。

entries.definition: A related verb in wend one's way, meaning to go.
entries.definitionCN: 相关动词，见于 wend one's way，义为行走。

entries.definition: To travel widely over a large area, often with ease.
entries.definitionCN: 在广大区域里自在游走。

entries.definition: To walk slowly and pleasantly, usually with company.
entries.definitionCN: 悠闲地、常与人同行地慢慢走。

entries.definition: To get lost or move off the proper place.
entries.definitionCN: 走失、离开应处之地。

entries.definition: To be carried along without control, often of the mind.
entries.definitionCN: 不受控制地被带走，常用于思绪。

normalIntro.en: Footsteps with no course, then a mind with no course, then a path with no straight line.
normalIntro.cn: 没有路线的脚步，接着是没有路线的思绪，最后是没有直线的路径。

normal.en: Wander and wonder differ by one letter: roam versus ask oneself.
normal.cn: wander 与 wonder 只差一个字母：漫游与想知道。

normal.en: Wander is regular: wander, wandered, wandered.
normal.cn: wander 是规则动词：wander、wandered、wandered。

normal.en: Wander off means stray away; wander from means leave the subject.
normal.cn: wander off 是走散，wander from 是偏离话题。

normal.en: A wanderer wanders; his wanderings fill a book.
normal.cn: a wanderer 漫游，他的 wanderings 可以写成书。

normal.en: Wend one's way shares the old root of wander.
normal.cn: wend one's way 与 wander 同出旧词根。

abstract.en: See feet turning left, then right, along lanes.
abstract.cn: 想象双脚在小巷里左拐右拐。

abstract.en: Hear a voice trail off into an unrelated story.
abstract.cn: 听一个声音慢慢拐进不相干的故事。

abstract.en: Picture a path drawing a long loop along a river bank.
abstract.cn: 想象小径沿河岸画出一个大弯。

examples.en: The children wandered in and out of the shops.
examples.cn: 孩子们在店铺之间进进出出地闲逛。

examples.en: Don't let your attention wander from the road.
examples.cn: 别让注意力离开路面。

examples.en: The stream wanders through the meadow.
examples.cn: 小溪蜿蜒穿过草甸。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弯的」——路是弯的，顺着弯弯的巷子一直走，就叫漫游。

root: 古英语 wandrian（漫游），同出日耳曼语词根（参 wend）；更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: No goal is the thread: feet roam, feet stray, thoughts drift, talk leaves the point, and roads wind.
sensesIntro.cn: 「没有目标」是这条线索：脚漫游、脚走散、思绪飘、话语离题、道路绕弯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steps turning corners with no destination.
core.cn: 核心意象：在巷子里拐来拐去、没有目的的脚步。

branches.en: The roaming branch: an afternoon in the old quarter.
branches.cn: 漫游分支：在老城区逛一个下午。

branches.en: The straying branch: a child lost by the bridge.
branches.cn: 走散分支：桥边走散的孩子。

branches.en: The mind branch: attention slipping during a lecture.
branches.cn: 思绪分支：听讲座时注意力滑走。

branches.en: The course branch: a talk off the point, a path along a bank.
branches.cn: 路线分支：离题的谈话与沿河的小径。

branches.en: The outing branch: a wander along the seafront.
branches.cn: 外出分支：沿海滨随便走走。

intro.en: Wand- is the roaming root; -er, -ing and -s do the building.
intro.cn: wand- 是「漫游」词根，词族由 -er、-ing、-s 搭建。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic and uncertain beyond that, so no Latin word is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 词根为日耳曼语，再往上不确定，故不列拉丁词条。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根携带无目的的移动。

items.example: It forms wander from the subject.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wander from the subject。

items.example: It forms wander around the town.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 wander around the town。

definition_zh: 病房；（城市的）区；受监护人；动词：挡开、避开
definition_en: a room or section of a hospital for patients, a district of a city, or to keep something away
core_image: 护士守在一间病人集中的房间里，门帘拉上，把外面的喧闹挡在门外
scene: 夜班的走廊很静，只有三号病房的灯还亮着。The children's ward was quiet, except for one child who could not sleep.
sceneCN: 这里 ward 是「病房」（第 1 个义项：医院里供病人集中的房间）；句意为儿童病房很安静，只有一个孩子睡不着。一间被帘子隔开、把喧闹挡在门外的房间，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：病房；城区；受监护的人（ward of court）

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -er 构成，义为「看守；狱警」
同一词根加 -en 构成，义为「管理员；看守人」
由 ward 与 robe 复合而成，义为「衣柜；全部衣物」
与 ward 同源，义为「守卫；卫兵」

senses.title: A hospital room for patients
senses.titleCN: 病房：医院里病人集中的房间
senses.definition: a large room in a hospital where several patients are cared for
senses.definitionCN: 医院中同时照料多位病人的大房间
senses.example: She was moved to a ward on the second floor.
senses.exampleCN: 她被转到了二楼的病房。
senses.why: The old verb meant to guard; a ward is the space kept and watched over by nurses.
senses.whyCN: 古义「看守」是这个字根；ward 就是护士守着、看着的那片空间。

senses.title: A district of a city
senses.titleCN: 城区：城市划分出的一个区域
senses.definition: an area of a city or town used as a unit for elections or local government
senses.definitionCN: 城市或城镇的一个区域，用作选举或地方行政单位
senses.example: Each ward elects one member of the council.
senses.exampleCN: 每个选区选出一名议会议员。
senses.why: A district is also a space kept and watched, this time by a local official.
senses.whyCN: 城区同样是被人看守、照管的一片空间，只不过看守者换成了地方官员。

senses.title: A person under protection
senses.titleCN: 受监护人：由他人或法庭监护的人
senses.definition: a person, especially a child, placed under the legal care of a guardian or a court
senses.definitionCN: 被置于监护人或法庭法律照管之下的人，尤指儿童
senses.example: As a ward of court, the boy needed a judge's permission to travel.
senses.exampleCN: 作为由法庭监护的孩子，他出国需要法官批准。
senses.why: Guardianship comes full circle here: the guarded space becomes the guarded person.
senses.whyCN: 监护义在这里走了一个圆：被看守的空间变成了被看守的人。

senses.title: To keep something away
senses.definition: in the phrase ward off, to prevent something harmful from reaching you
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 ward off，指阻止有害之物接近自己
senses.example: She waved her hand to ward off the flies.
senses.exampleCN: 她挥手把苍蝇挡开。
senses.why: The verb restores the original guarding action: the arm and the charm stand between you and harm.
senses.whyCN: 动词恢复了最初的看守动作：手臂与护符拦在你和伤害之间。

senses.title: As a suffix in compound words
senses.titleCN: 作后缀：构成方向或对象的复合词
senses.definition: used as a suffix in words such as homeward and backward, marking direction
senses.definitionCN: 用作 homeward、backward 等词的后缀，表示方向
senses.example: The road homeward was longer than he remembered.
senses.exampleCN: 回家的路比他记忆中的更长。
senses.why: The same Old English element shifted from 'keeping watch' to 'turning toward', a change the etymologists still discuss.
senses.whyCN: 同一古英语成分从「守望」转向「朝向」，这一变化至今仍为词源学者讨论。

intro.en: Ward is an Old English word for keeping watch, and the modern senses all grow out of guarded space and guarded people.
intro.cn: ward 是古英语中表示「守望」的词，现代各义项都由「被看守的空间」与「被看守的人」生长出来。

items.en: Weard meant 'a watch, a guarding'; the verb weardian meant to guard or occupy.
items.cn: weard 意为「守望、守卫」，动词 weardian 意为看守或占据。

items.en: Related forms in Old Saxon and Old High German share the guarding sense, so the root is very old.
items.cn: 古撒克逊语与古高地德语中的相关形式同样表示看守，可见这一词根极为古老。

items.en: The word came to name a guarded place: a district watched by an officer, and later a room watched by nurses.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐指被看守的地方：先是由官员管辖的城区，后是由护士照看的房间。

items.en: By c. 1300 a ward of court was a minor under the court's protection, the guarded person.
items.cn: 约在 1300 年，ward of court 指受法庭保护、被照管的未成年人。

items.en: The phrase ward off kept the original action alive, while the -ward suffix developed its direction sense.
items.cn: 短语 ward off 保住了最初的动作义，而 -ward 后缀则发展出方向义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers guarding words of the same root; the near-meaning group gathers hospital rooms and city districts.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的看守类词；近义组收病房与城区的相关说法。

entries.definition: To protect or watch over; the French-shaped twin of ward.
entries.definitionCN: 动词或名词，义为「守卫、卫兵」，是 ward 的法语形孪生词。

entries.definition: An official who watches over a building, a park or prisoners.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理员、看守长」，指看守建筑、园区或囚犯的人。

entries.definition: A prison officer; the person who does the guarding.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「狱警、看守」。

entries.definition: In the direction of; -ward here marks direction, not guarding.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「朝向」，此处的 -ward 表方向而非看守。

entries.definition: A place for medical advice or treatment, often smaller than a hospital ward.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「诊所」，通常比病房所在科室小。

entries.definition: An area of a town or country, the everyday word beside ward.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「地区、区域」，是 ward 在城区义上的日常说法。

entries.definition: To push away or look after oneself; often in fend off.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挡开、照料自己」，多用于 fend off。

entries.definition: To drive something back by force; stronger than ward off.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「击退」，比 ward off 语气更强。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English weard and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 weard，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: ward and guard are one word in two shapes: one English, one French.
normal.cn: ward 与 guard 是同一个词的两副面孔：一个英语形，一个法语形。

normal.en: A ward is a space watched over; a warden is the person who watches.
normal.cn: ward 是被看守的空间；warden 是看守的人。

normal.en: Ward off keeps the original meaning: hold the harm outside.
normal.cn: ward off 保留了本义：把伤害挡在外面。

normal.en: The children's ward, the maternity ward: names for groups of patients in one room.
normal.cn: 儿童病房、产科病房：都是同一间房里一群病人的名字。

normal.en: Each city ward elects its own councillor.
normal.cn: 城市的每个选区各自选出议员。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain drawn across a hospital bay: inside is watched, outside is shut out, and both are ward.
abstract.cn: 想象病房里拉上一道帘子：里面被照看，外面被隔开，两者都是 ward。

abstract.en: The word moves from the watchman to the place watched, and then to the person watched over.
abstract.cn: 这个词从守望者移到被守望的地方，再移到被照看的人。

abstract.en: Warding off is the smallest form of guarding: one raised arm against a fly.
abstract.cn: 挡开是最小形式的看守：一条抬起的手臂挡住一只苍蝇。

examples.en: The nurse checked every bed in the ward before midnight.
examples.cn: 护士在午夜前查看了病房里的每一张床。

examples.en: He lit a fire to ward off the cold.
examples.cn: 他生起火来御寒。

examples.en: The city is divided into twelve wards for local elections.
examples.cn: 这座城市为地方选举划分为十二个选区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我（war）的（d）」——我的地盘我守着，一间病人住着的房间：病房；守望

root: 古英语 weard「守望、守卫」，动词 weardian「看守」；与 guard 同源，-ward 后缀亦出自同一成分；派生词有 warden、warder、wardrobe。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of ward travel from the guarding act to the place guarded, the district, the person guarded, the act of keeping harm away, and finally the direction suffix.
sensesIntro.cn: ward 的五个义项从看守动作出发，依次走到被看守的空间、城区、被看守的人、把伤害挡开的动作，最后是表方向的后缀。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curtain drawn across a hospital bay, the inside watched, the outside shut away.
core.cn: 核心意象：病房里拉上的帘子，里面被照看，外面被隔开。

branches.en: ROOM LINE: the space nurses keep watch over.
branches.cn: 房间线：护士守望的那片空间。

branches.en: MAP LINE: the city is cut into wards, each watched by an officer.
branches.cn: 地图线：城市被切成若干区，每区由官员管辖。

branches.en: PERSON LINE: the guarded space becomes a guarded child.
branches.cn: 人物线：被看守的空间变成了被照看的孩子。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: ward off brings back the original raised arm.
branches.cn: 动作线：ward off 带回最初抬起的手臂。

branches.en: SUFFIX LINE: the same element turns into a direction marker.
branches.cn: 后缀线：同一成分转为方向标记。

intro.en: Ward is a native Old English word; its 'affixes' are really its own suffixes, which also appear across the language.
intro.cn: ward 是本族古英语词；这里所谓的词缀其实是它自身的后缀成分，同样通行于其他词中。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 仓库；货栈；把（货物）存入仓库；大型仓储式商店
definition_en: a large building where goods are stored, or to place goods in such a building
core_image: 一栋没有橱窗的大房子，里面只有货架、托盘与叉车，货进来后等着再出去
scene: 叉车把托盘推进高大的货架深处，卷帘门在身后落下，这些货要等到下一批订单才会被取出。The warehouse holds the pallets until the shops place their orders.
sceneCN: 卷帘门在叉车后落下，整托货物被推进高架深处，等待着下一批订单；句中的 warehouse 指「存放货物、等待再运出的大建筑」（第 1 个义项：以储藏为主要功能的建筑）。图中可辨识物件：叉车、托盘、高货架、卷帘门。

derivatives.zh: 仓储；仓储业
已存入仓库的
仓库管理员；仓储工人

senses.title: A building for storing goods
senses.titleCN: 存放货物、等待再运出的大建筑
senses.definition: a large building in which goods are kept until they are sold or moved on
senses.definitionCN: 货物在售出或转运之前被存放其中的大型建筑
senses.example: The warehouse holds the pallets until the shops place their orders.
senses.exampleCN: 仓库持有这些托盘，直到店铺下单为止。
senses.why: the compound joins the old word for goods with the word for a house, so the name says exactly what the building is for.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把指货物的旧词与指房屋的词拼在一起，名称直接说明了建筑的用途。

senses.title: To store goods in such a building
senses.definition: to place goods in a warehouse for keeping
senses.definitionCN: 把货物放入仓库保存
senses.example: The grain was warehoused until prices improved.
senses.exampleCN: 谷物被存入仓库，等价格好转再出。
senses.why: the building's name became a verb for putting things into it, a common shift in English.
senses.whyCN: 建筑的名称变成了「把东西放进去」的动词，这在英语中很常见。

senses.title: A large no-frills shop
senses.titleCN: 以仓储式陈列经营的大型商店
senses.definition: a large shop that displays goods on pallets in a plain building, often selling to members
senses.definitionCN: 在朴素建筑里以托盘方式陈列货物、常面向会员销售的大型商店
senses.example: The warehouse club sells flour by the fifty-kilo sack.
senses.exampleCN: 仓储式会员店按五十公斤一袋卖面粉。
senses.why: the shop borrows the building's look: goods sit on pallets, the room is plain, and the price is low.
senses.whyCN: 这种商店借用了仓库的样子：货放在托盘上，空间朴素，价格低廉。

senses.title: The dispatch end of online selling
senses.titleCN: 网络零售的配送仓储中心
senses.definition: a centre where goods are stored and packed for delivery to individual customers
senses.definitionCN: 存放货物并打包、直接送往个人顾客的中心
senses.example: The online seller runs one warehouse for the whole country.
senses.exampleCN: 这家网商在全国只用一个仓储中心。
senses.why: when the shop moves online, the warehouse takes over the packing that the shop counter once did.
senses.whyCN: 商店搬到网上后，原本由柜台完成的打包工作转由仓库承担。

senses.title: A customs-controlled store
senses.titleCN: 受海关监管、关税暂缓的保税仓库
senses.definition: a secured store where imported goods may be held before duty is paid
senses.definitionCN: 进口货物在缴纳关税前可存放其中的受监管仓库
senses.example: The wine stayed in a bonded warehouse for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 这批葡萄酒在保税仓库里放了两年。
senses.why: the state needs a place where goods are physically present but not yet legally imported, and calls it a warehouse.
senses.whyCN: 国家需要一个地方，让货物实际在场但在法律上尚未进口，于是称之为仓库。

senses.title: A store of data in computing
senses.titleCN: 计算机系统中的数据仓库
senses.definition: a central store that holds data gathered from many systems for analysis
senses.definitionCN: 汇集来自多个系统的数据、供分析之用的中央存储
senses.example: The data warehouse pulls figures from every branch.
senses.exampleCN: 数据仓库从每个分支机构抽取数据。
senses.why: computing reuses the building: data is stacked and kept, then drawn out when needed.
senses.whyCN: 计算机领域复用了这座建筑：数据被堆起来保存，需要时再取出。

senses.title: Storage as a business
senses.titleCN: 作为行业的仓储与仓储设施
senses.definition: the business of storing goods for others, or the space used for it
senses.definitionCN: 替他人存放货物的行业，或用于此事的空间
senses.example: Warehousing near the port is cheaper than inland.
senses.exampleCN: 港口附近的仓储比内陆便宜。
senses.why: once storage is sold as a service, the building's name extends to the trade and to the space itself.
senses.whyCN: 当储存作为服务出售时，建筑名就扩展到整个行业以及所占的空间。

senses.title: A store of memories or records
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：存放记忆或资料的储藏处
senses.definition: a place or system that keeps large amounts of memories, records or material
senses.definitionCN: 保存大量记忆、记录或材料的场所或系统
senses.example: The archive is a warehouse of the city's ordinary voices.
senses.exampleCN: 这座档案馆存放着这座城市普通人的声音。
senses.why: the physical image survives without walls: whatever is kept in quantity can be called a warehouse.
senses.whyCN: 实体意象在没有墙壁时仍然成立：任何被大量保存的东西都可以叫仓库。

intro.en: Warehouse is a native English compound of ware 'goods' and house, both inherited from Old English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: warehouse 是英语本族复合词，由 ware「货物」与 house「房屋」构成，两者都承自古代英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Waru meant 'goods, articles of merchandise, a kept thing', and its descendant ware survives in wares and in compounds.
items.cn: waru 意为「货物、商品、被保存之物」，其后代 ware 仍存于「货品」及若干复合词中。

items.en: Hūs meant 'house, dwelling, shelter', the direct ancestor of house.
items.cn: hūs 意为「房屋、住所、遮蔽处」，是 house 的直接祖先。

items.en: Ware plus house named a building where goods were kept, and the word is recorded from the medieval period.
items.cn: 「货物」加「房屋」指存放货物的建筑，这个词在中世纪已有记载。

items.en: With overseas trade the warehouse became a port institution, with receipts, customs control and bonded storage.
items.cn: 随着海外贸易，仓库成为港口制度的一部分，出现仓单、海关监管与保税存放。

items.en: The twentieth century added the warehouse club and the distribution centre, and computing added the data warehouse.
items.cn: 二十世纪添了仓储式会员店与配送中心，计算机领域又添了数据仓库。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same two halves or their near kin; group two holds names for places that store things.
note.cn: 第一组由同样的两半或其近亲构成；第二组是存放物品的场所之名。

entries.definition: An old word for manufactured goods or articles for sale, still heard in wares and earthenware.
entries.definitionCN: 指制成品或待售物品的旧词，仍见于「货品」与「陶器」等说法。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for a dwelling or building; in the compound it simply supplies the building.
entries.definitionCN: 指住所或建筑的常用词；在复合词里只提供「建筑」这一层。

entries.definition: The business or process of storing goods; the longer form names the activity, not the building.
entries.definitionCN: 存放货物的业务或过程；较长的形式指活动，而非建筑。

entries.definition: A worker who handles goods in a warehouse; the compound plus a person suffix names the job.
entries.definitionCN: 在仓库中搬运货物的人；复合词加表人后缀构成职业名。

entries.definition: A place where vehicles are kept or goods are received for transport; it stresses movement rather than storage.
entries.definitionCN: 停放车辆或接收待运货物之处；强调运输而非储存。

entries.definition: A building for storing things, close in meaning but without the commercial and customs associations.
entries.definitionCN: 存放物品的建筑，意思接近，但不带商业与海关的联想。

entries.definition: The room at the back of a shop where reserve stock is kept; much smaller than a warehouse.
entries.definitionCN: 商店后面存放备用存货的房间，比仓库小得多。

entries.definition: A large facility that sorts and sends goods onward; storage is a means, not the purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 对货物进行分拣并继续发运的大型设施；储存只是手段而非目的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two real halves, the real modern formats and the real customs phrase.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的两半、真实的现代业态与真实的海关说法。

normal.en: Ware plus house: a house for goods, not for people.
normal.cn: 「货物」加「房屋」：给货住的房子，不是给人住的。

normal.en: The family runs warehouse, warehousing, warehoused and warehouseman.
normal.cn: 同族词包括仓库、仓储、已入库的与仓库工人。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: bonded warehouse, warehouse club, data warehouse.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这个词：保税仓库、仓储式会员店、数据仓库。

normal.en: A warehouse has no shop window; its whole purpose is to keep things out of view.
normal.cn: 仓库没有橱窗；它的全部用途就是把东西放在看不见的地方。

normal.en: Online selling turned the warehouse into the busiest part of the shop.
normal.cn: 网络销售把仓库变成了店铺里最忙碌的部分。

abstract.en: Picture a building with no windows and a door that only opens for trucks.
abstract.cn: 想象一栋没有窗、门只为货车而开的建筑。

abstract.en: Picture shelves that hold seasons of goods in silence.
abstract.cn: 想象一排排货架，静默地囤着好几个季节的货。

abstract.en: Picture a mind that stacks memories on pallets and fetches them years later.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗心把记忆码在托盘上，多年后再取出来。

examples.en: The warehouse is full, so new stock waits on the trucks.
examples.cn: 仓库已满，新货只能在车上等着。

examples.en: Goods in a bonded warehouse are stored before duty is paid.
examples.cn: 保税仓库中的货物在缴税前存放。

examples.en: The company warehoused the surplus rather than discount it.
examples.cn: 公司把余货入库，而不是打折卖掉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ware（货物）+ house（房子）」——放货物的房子 → 仓库

root: 英语本族复合词：ware（货物，古英语 waru）＋house（房屋，古英语 hūs），字面即「放货的房子」，与拉丁语无同族关系。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with a plain building for goods and then follow the same shape into shops, delivery centres, customs control, computing and finally into any store of kept things.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一座放货的朴素建筑开始，再让同一形状走进商店、配送中心、海关监管、计算机，最后成为任何储藏之所。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a windowless building where pallets wait behind a rolling door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一栋没有窗的建筑，托盘在卷帘门后等待。

branches.en: THE BUILDING AND THE TRADE: storage is first a place, then a service sold by the square metre.
branches.cn: 建筑与行业：储存先是一个场所，后来成为按面积出售的服务。

branches.en: PUT IN AND SEND OUT: the verb and the delivery centre are the two directions of the same door.
branches.cn: 放入与发出：动词与配送中心是同一扇门的两个方向。

branches.en: THE LOOK BECOMES A SHOP: pallets and plain aisles are turned into a retail format.
branches.cn: 样子变成商店：托盘与朴素通道被改造成一种零售业态。

branches.en: HELD BY LAW: goods may sit physically present yet not legally entered.
branches.cn: 受法律扣留：货物可以实际在场，却在法律上尚未入境。

branches.en: NO WALLS NEEDED: data and memories are stacked and fetched in exactly the same shape.
branches.cn: 无需墙壁：数据与记忆以完全相同的形状被堆放和取出。

intro.en: The word is two Old English nouns joined, so there is no Latin affix to read.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个古英语名词并合而成，因此没有拉丁词缀可拆。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entries apply: both halves are inherited Germanic words.
latinIntro.cn: 不适用拉丁条目：两半都是承继的日耳曼语词。

items.example: The house has no windows on the street.
items.exampleCN: 这栋房子临街一面没有窗。

items.example: The warehouse holds the winter stock.

items.meaning: to store in such a building
items.example: They warehoused the grain for a year.
Warehousing takes space near the port.
items.exampleCN: 仓储需要在港口附近占用空间。

items.example: The goods were warehoused until spring.

items.exampleCN: 仓库工人检查了每个托盘。

items.exampleCN: 仓储式会员店按大包装出售。
