definition_zh: 战争；作战；（尤指）进行战争的行为与方式
definition_en: the activity of fighting a war, especially the manner in which armed conflict is conducted
core_image: 泥泞的旷野上，翻倒的辎重车还在冒烟，地平线被火光染红，半埋的头盔露出边缘
scene: 泥泞的旷野上，翻倒的辎重车还在冒烟，地平线被火光染红，半埋的头盔露出边缘。Modern warfare depends on drones as much as on infantry.
sceneCN: 这里 warfare 指「进行战争的行为与方式」（第 1 个义项：以有组织武装力量交战的整体活动，尤指其打法）；句意为现代战争对无人机的依赖不亚于对步兵的依赖。图中可辨识物件：翻倒的辎重车、升起的烟、被火光染红的地平线、半埋的头盔。

pos.zh: 战争；作战（一般不可数；指某一类作战方式时可加修饰语，如 guerrilla warfare）

derivatives.zh: 战争；打仗（古北法语 werre 出自法兰克语 *werra「混乱、争斗」，语义偏移为「有组织的武装冲突」，与拉丁 bellum 无关）
战士（war 加古法语施事后缀 -eur，经 werreur 进入英语，语义偏移为「上阵作战的人」）
好战的（war 加古英语相似后缀 -lic，语义偏移为「带有战争气息的」）
战时（war 与 time 的英语复合，time 源自古英语 tima「时间」，语义偏移为「战争持续的时期」）
军舰（war 与 ship 的英语复合，ship 源自古英语 scip「船」，语义偏移为「为作战而建的船」）
车费；行程；过活（古英语 faru「旅程、队伍」，语义偏移为「出行、旅费、进食」，正是 warfare 后半的来源）

senses.title: The conduct of armed conflict
senses.definition: the activity of fighting with organized armed forces, especially the way it is carried out
senses.definitionCN: 以有组织的武装力量交战这一活动，尤指其进行方式
senses.example: Modern warfare depends on drones as much as on infantry.
senses.exampleCN: 现代战争对无人机的依赖不亚于对步兵的依赖。
senses.why: War can mean the declared state; warfare names the doing of it, so the word describes activity rather than a legal condition.
senses.whyCN: war 可以指宣示的状态，warfare 命名的是「做」这件事，因此它描述活动而非法律状态。

senses.title: A state of war between parties
senses.definition: the condition in which two or more states or factions are openly or formally at war
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个国家或派别公开或正式处于交战之中的状况
senses.example: The two republics drifted into warfare after the border patrols clashed.
senses.exampleCN: 边境巡逻队冲突之后，两个共和国逐渐滑入战争状态。
senses.why: The second element once meant a journey or expedition, so the word can name a whole stretch of hostile going, not only a battle.
senses.whyCN: 后半部分原指旅程或出征，因此这个词可以命名一整段敌对行程，而不只是一场战斗。

senses.title: A named type of war
senses.definition: a labeled mode of fighting, such as conventional, guerrilla, naval, chemical or cyber warfare
senses.definitionCN: 有标签的作战方式，如常规战、游击战、海战、化学战或网络战
senses.example: Guerrilla warfare bogged down the occupying army for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 游击战让占领军陷于泥潭达十年之久。
senses.why: Types branch off naturally because warfare names a manner of fighting, and manners can always be labeled.
senses.whyCN: 类型会自然分出来，因为 warfare 命名的是打法，而打法总能被贴上标签。

senses.title: Military operations taken as a whole
senses.definition: the collective name for campaigns, raids, sieges and patrols conducted by an armed force
senses.definitionCN: 对一支武装力量所进行的战役、突袭、围攻与巡逻的整体称呼
senses.example: The museum's maps record the warfare of an entire campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 馆里的地图记录了整场战役的军事行动。
senses.why: Once many operations are seen together, the mass of them takes the same name as the activity that produced them.
senses.whyCN: 当许多行动被放在一起看时，这一大堆行动就与产生它们的活动同名。

senses.title: Figurative struggle
senses.definition: a hostile contest waged with pressure rather than weapons, as in class warfare or price warfare
senses.definitionCN: 以压力而非武器进行的敌对较量，如阶级对抗或价格战
senses.example: The two chains waged price warfare until smaller shops closed.
senses.exampleCN: 两家连锁店打价格战，直到小店纷纷关门。
senses.why: Any contest that feels like a campaign borrows the word, whether the weapons are prices, laws or insults.
senses.whyCN: 任何感觉像战役的较量都会借用这个词，无论武器是价格、法律还是恶语。

senses.title: The art of war
senses.definition: the study of strategy, logistics and tactics as a disciplined craft
senses.definitionCN: 把战略、后勤与战术当作一门有章法的技艺来研究
senses.example: He studied warfare at the staff college for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在参谋学院学了两年战争艺术。
senses.why: The conduct of war can be taught and examined, so the activity turns into a subject with its own rules.
senses.whyCN: 作战可以被教授与考核，因此这项活动变成一门有自身规则学问。

senses.title: The destruction war leaves behind
senses.definition: the ruin of towns, fields and lives that armed conflict produces, often spoken of as a mass
senses.definitionCN: 武装冲突造成的城镇、田野与生命的毁坏，常被当作一整片来谈论
senses.example: Whole districts still show the scars of that warfare.
senses.exampleCN: 整片城区至今仍留着那场战争造成的伤痕。
senses.why: The object of the word can be the wreckage rather than the fighting, because destruction is what warfare leaves visible.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的所指可以是废墟而非战斗，因为战争留下的可见之物正是破坏。

senses.title: Open conflict between groups
senses.definition: hostility between gangs, factions or communities, short of a declared war
senses.definitionCN: 帮派、派系或社区之间的敌对，尚未达到宣战程度
senses.example: Police blame gang warfare for the shootings in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 警方把该区的枪击归因于帮派争斗。
senses.why: Where organized groups fight without states, the same word describes the smaller war without any legal claim.
senses.whyCN: 当有组织的群体在没有国家的情况下打斗，同一个词就用来描述这场规模更小的战争，不涉任何法律主张。

intro.en: War comes from a Frankish word of strife, not from Latin bellum, while the second element is Old English faru 'journey, troop'. The compound is native English built on a borrowed first word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: war 来自法兰克语中表示争斗的词，并非拉丁 bellum；后半部分是古英语 faru「旅程、队伍」。整个复合词是英语本土构造，只借了第一个词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Werra meant 'confusion, strife, discord'; it is a reconstructed form, written with an asterisk because no text records it directly.
items.cn: werra 意为「混乱、争斗、不和」；它属重构形式，写作时加星号，因为没有任何文本直接记录它。

items.en: Old North French took the Frankish word as werre and passed it to English after the Norman settlement.
items.cn: 古北法语把法兰克语这个词吸收为 werre，并在诺曼定居之后传入英语。

items.en: English spelled it werre and warre before settling on war, and the word never came from Latin bellum.
items.cn: 英语先写作 werre、warre，后来定为 war；这个词从来不出自拉丁 bellum。

items.en: Faru meant 'a journey, an expedition, a troop on the move', and it is the same word that survives in fare.
items.cn: faru 意为「旅程、出征、行进中的队伍」，与今天仍存的 fare 是同一个词。

items.en: The compound of war plus fare named the waging of war, literally a going to war with troops.
items.cn: war 与 fare 的复合词命名「进行战争」，字面就是带着队伍出征。

items.en: Source uncertain (reconstruction and first date): werra is a reconstruction and its deeper origin is source uncertain; the first English use of the compound is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（重构形式与首见年代）：werra 属重构形式，其更早来源属来源不确定；这个复合词在英语中最早的使用只能大致系年。

note.en: Group one holds the two elements that make the compound plus near-identical words built on them, which are often read as if they meant the same thing; group two holds other names for organized fighting.
note.cn: 第一组是构成该复合词的两个部分及其上长出的形近词，常被误读为同义；第二组是有组织交战的其他名称。

entries.definition: The conflict itself or its declared condition; warfare is the conduct, not the declaration.
entries.definitionCN: 指冲突本身或宣示的状态；warfare 指进行方式，而非宣示。

entries.definition: A journey, a passenger's ticket or the price of travel; the element once meant exactly a journey, not a cost.
entries.definitionCN: 指行程、车票或旅费；这一词素原义正是「旅程」，并非「费用」。

entries.definition: Well plus fare, 'the state of faring well'; it is not war plus fare and has nothing to do with fighting.
entries.definitionCN: 由 well 加 fare 构成，意为「过得好」的状态；它不是 war 加 fare，与打仗无关。

entries.definition: The fighter, built on the same war stock with an agent suffix; it names a person, not an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指战斗者，由同一 war 词干加施事后缀构成；它指人，不指活动。

entries.definition: Actual fighting between forces; combat is the clash, whereas warfare is the whole activity and its manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指部队之间的实际交火；combat 是那一下碰撞，warfare 则是整体活动及其打法。

entries.definition: Any prolonged hostility, from a border skirmish to a trade dispute; it need not involve armies at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何持续的敌对，从边境小规模冲突到贸易争端；可完全不涉及军队。

entries.definition: The official term for acts of war once they begin; it belongs to communiques rather than to description.
entries.definitionCN: 对开战行为的正式称呼；它属于公报语言，而非描写语言。

entries.definition: One engagement between forces; warfare contains many battles and outlives all of them.
entries.definitionCN: 指部队之间的一次交战；warfare 包含许多场战斗，并比它们持续更久。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Werra 'strife' came from Frankish, not from Latin bellum, so war and the Latin words for war are not relatives.
normal.cn: werra「争斗」来自法兰克语，而非拉丁 bellum，因此 war 与拉丁语中表示战争的词并非同族。

normal.en: The second element is Old English faru 'journey, troop', the same word that survives in fare and farewell.
normal.cn: 后半部分是古英语 faru「旅程、队伍」，与 fare、farewell 中留存的是同一个词。

normal.en: The compound is a going to war: war plus fare, not war plus a ticket price.
normal.cn: 这个复合词意为出征：war 加 fare，而不是 war 加票价。

normal.en: The family runs war, warrior, warlike, wartime, warship, warfare.
normal.cn: 同族词依次是 war、warrior、warlike、wartime、warship、warfare。

normal.en: Collocations label the kinds: guerrilla warfare, chemical warfare, naval warfare, modern warfare.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出类型：游击战、化学战、海战、现代战争。

abstract.en: Picture a column of carts rolling out at dawn, dust rising behind them in one long line.
abstract.cn: 想象一列车队在黎明出发，扬起的尘土在车后拉成长长一条。

abstract.en: Picture a map with red arrows drawn over it, arrows that stop at a river and never resume.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上画着红色箭头，箭头在一条河边停住，再没有继续。

abstract.en: Picture a field of wheat with a single track cut through it, straight as a ruler.
abstract.cn: 想象一片麦田被一道笔直如尺的车辙从中划开。

examples.en: The manual treats warfare as a craft with rules, not as a series of heroic episodes.
examples.cn: 这本手册把作战当作一门有规则的技艺，而不是一串英雄插曲。

examples.en: Drought and warfare drove the same families across the border in the same season.
examples.cn: 旱灾与战乱在同一个季节把同一批家庭赶过了边境。

examples.en: Economists now speak of warfare between platforms over the same customers.
examples.cn: 经济学家如今谈论平台之间为争夺同一批顾客而展开的战争。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「war（打）+ fare（走一趟）」——带着队伍出去打一趟 → 战争、作战；fare 这里是「行程」不是「费用」

root: war 来自古北法语 werre，源自法兰克语 *werra「混乱、争斗」（重构形式），并非拉丁 bellum；-fare 来自古英语 faru「旅程、队伍」，与 fare、farewell 同族。warfare 不是 war 加 fare「费用」，而是「出征打仗」。*werra 更早来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one expedition: troops go out to fight, and that going is then read as the conduct itself, a state, a labeled type, the mass of operations, a metaphor, an art, the ruin left, and finally any group's open conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一次出征展开：队伍出去作战，这次出行再依次被读作作战本身、战争状态、贴标签的类型、行动的总和、比喻、技艺、留下的废墟，最后是任何群体的公开冲突。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a column of carts and troops on the move, and the ground behind them already burnt.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支车队与队伍正在开拔，身后的地面已经烧过。

branches.en: DOING AND BEING: the activity of fighting and the condition of being at war are one event seen as motion or as state.
branches.cn: 动作与状态：交战的活动与处于战争中的状态，是同一事件被看作运动或状态。

branches.en: MANNER AND MASS: a labeled way of fighting and the sum of all operations both describe how the war is waged.
branches.cn: 方式与总和：有标签的打法与所有行动的总和，都在描述战争如何被进行。

branches.en: METAPHOR AND CRAFT: any hard contest borrows the word, and the real thing can be studied as an art.
branches.cn: 比喻与技艺：任何激烈较量都借用这个词，而真实战争可以被当作技艺来研究。

branches.en: THE WRECKAGE: what remains visible of warfare is the ruin, so the word can name the damage itself.
branches.cn: 废墟：战争可见的遗留就是毁坏，因此这个词也能指破坏本身。

branches.en: SMALLER WAR: groups without states repeat the whole shape at the scale of a street.
branches.cn: 更小的战争：没有国家的群体在街区的规模上重演整个结构。

intro.en: The word is a native compound with a borrowed first element: a Frankish noun of strife, an Old English noun of journey, and a second element that behaves almost like a suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词是本土复合词，只有第一个成分是借来的：一个法兰克语「争斗」名词、一个古英语「旅程」名词，以及一个作用近乎后缀的第二成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin kin here: war is Frankish in origin rather than Latin bellum, and fare is Old English, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁同族：war 源自法兰克语而非拉丁 bellum，fare 属古英语，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: The asterisk marks a form reconstructed from later evidence.
items.exampleCN: 星号表示这是依据后世材料重构的形式。

items.example: The French form is the direct bridge to English.
items.exampleCN: 这个法语形式是通往英语的直接桥梁。

items.example: English shortened the borrowed noun to one syllable.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个借来的名词缩成一个音节。

items.meaning: a journey, an expedition, a troop
items.example: The noun supplies the going that the compound needs.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供复合词所需的「出行」义。

items.meaning: to travel; a journey; the price of travel
items.example: The modern noun keeps the journey and adds the cost.
items.exampleCN: 现代名词保留「行程」，又添上「花费」。

items.example: Welfare and warfare both end in this element, though only one begins with war.
items.exampleCN: welfare 与 warfare 都以这个成分结尾，尽管只有一个以 war 开头。

items.example: The compound names the going out to fight, not the price of a ticket.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词命名的是出征作战，而不是票价。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun of strife into a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把「争斗」名词变成一个人。

items.meaningCN: 具有战争性质的；好战的
items.example: The suffix makes an adjective of manner out of the noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由名词造出表示性质的形容词。

definition_zh: 温暖的；暖和的；热情的；动词：使暖和、加热
definition_en: fairly hot in a pleasant way, friendly and enthusiastic, or to make something slightly hotter
core_image: 双手捧住一杯刚倒的热茶，指尖一点点回暖
scene: 冬天的厨房窗户起了雾，灶上的水正冒着热气。She wrapped both hands around the warm cup and stopped shivering.
sceneCN: 这里 warm 是「温暖的、暖和的」（第 1 个义项：温度适中而令人舒适）；句意为她双手捧住暖和的杯子，不再发抖。捧着热杯回温的感觉，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：温暖的；暖和的；热情的、亲切的
动词：使暖和；加热；变得热情

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀 -th 构成，义为「温暖；热情」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「温暖地；热情地」
由比较级转为名词，义为「加热器；暖手器」
加 -ing 构成，义为「变暖；加温」

senses.title: Pleasantly hot
senses.titleCN: 温暖的：温度舒服地偏高
senses.definition: fairly hot, especially in a way that feels pleasant rather than uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 温度较高，尤其令人舒适而不难受
senses.example: The bread was still warm from the oven.
senses.exampleCN: 面包刚从炉子里出来，还热着。
senses.why: Old English wearm described a moderate heat, and the word has always kept that comfort, not the extreme.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 wearm 指适中的热度，这个词一直保留着舒适感，而不指极端。

senses.title: Of clothing or shelter
senses.titleCN: 保暖的：衣物或住处不易散失热量
senses.definition: keeping the body heat in, as of clothes, rooms or bedding
senses.definitionCN: 能留住体温的，如衣服、房间或被褥
senses.example: Take a warm coat; the wind is sharp tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 带上件厚外套，今晚风很刺骨。
senses.why: The same moderate heat is held close to the body, so the adjective moves from air to clothing.
senses.whyCN: 同一种适中的热度被留在身体旁边，于是形容词从空气转移到衣物上。

senses.title: Friendly and enthusiastic
senses.titleCN: 热情的：态度亲切而热烈
senses.definition: showing friendliness, affection or enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 表现出友善、亲近或热忱
senses.example: They gave the visitors a warm welcome at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在门口热情地欢迎来访者。
senses.why: Warmth in the body became warmth in manner: a person who makes you comfortable is metaphorically warm.
senses.whyCN: 身上的温暖变成了态度上的温暖：让人感到舒适的人，在比喻意义上就是 warm。

senses.title: To make slightly hotter
senses.definition: to make something warmer, or to become warmer
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变暖，或自身变暖
senses.example: Warm the milk gently before adding the honey.
senses.exampleCN: 加蜂蜜之前先把牛奶稍稍加热。
senses.why: The adjective turns into the action that produces it: heat is applied a little at a time.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成产生它的动作：热被一点一点地加上去。

senses.title: To become friendly toward
senses.titleCN: 变得喜欢：对某人某事生出好感
senses.definition: in phrases like warm to, to begin to like or feel friendly toward something
senses.definitionCN: 用于 warm to 等短语，指开始喜欢或对某事产生好感
senses.example: The audience warmed to her after the second song.
senses.exampleCN: 第二首歌之后，观众开始喜欢上她。
senses.why: Friendliness is again heat, but now rising slowly, as a cold room warms up.
senses.whyCN: 友善再度成了热，只不过这次是慢慢升起的，像一间冷屋子渐渐暖起来。

intro.en: Warm is an old Germanic word, and its relatives run all through northern Europe.
intro.cn: warm 是古老的日耳曼语词，它的同源词遍布北欧各语言。

items.en: Wearm meant 'warm, not cold', and also appeared in compounds for warm-hearted feeling.
items.cn: wearm 意为「暖的、不冷的」，也出现在表示热心的复合词中。

items.en: The root is reconstructed as a word for being warm; German warm and Dutch warm are exact cognates.
items.cn: 这个词根被重构为「温暖」之义；德语 warm 与荷兰语 warm 是精确同源词。

items.en: Deeper connections to Latin formus 'warm' are debated, and the further origin is uncertain.
items.cn: 它与拉丁语 formus「暖的」之间更深的关系仍有争议，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The spelling settled as warm, and the verb use, to warm something, was already common.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 warm，动词用法「使暖和」当时已很常见。

items.en: Idioms extended the word: warm up for exercise, warm to an idea, a warm welcome.
items.cn: 习语进一步扩展了它：warm up 热身、warm to 产生好感、warm welcome 热情欢迎。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers temperature words close in shape; the near-meaning group gathers degrees and kinds of heat.
note.cn: 形近组收形状相近的温度词；近义组收不同程度与不同性质的热。

entries.definition: The noun for the quality of being warm, and for friendly feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「温暖；热情」，指暖的性质与友善情感。

entries.definition: A device or garment that keeps something warm; also the comparative.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指保暖的器具或衣物；也是比较级形式。

entries.definition: The adverb for doing something in a warm or friendly way.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「温暖地；热情地」。

entries.definition: Gentle exercise before a sport or performance.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「热身运动」。

entries.definition: At a high temperature, often uncomfortable; far stronger than warm.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「热的」，温度高且常令人不适，比 warm 强得多。

entries.definition: Only slightly warm, and by extension unenthusiastic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「微温的」，引申为「不热心的」。

entries.definition: Snug and comfortable; the feeling of warmth rather than its degree.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「舒适暖和的」，侧重感受而非温度。

entries.definition: Made hot deliberately; also describes an angry argument.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「加热的」，也形容激烈的争论。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English wearm and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 wearm，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: warm sits between cool and hot: pleasant heat, not a burn.
normal.cn: warm 位于 cool 与 hot 之间：是舒服的热，不会烫。

normal.en: A warm welcome borrows the body's comfort for the manners.
normal.cn: a warm welcome 借身体的舒适来形容待客之道。

normal.en: Warm up first, or the muscles will complain.
normal.cn: 先 warm up 热身，否则肌肉会抱怨。

normal.en: Lukewarm adds a lukewarm middle: only slightly warm, and not keen.
normal.cn: lukewarm 在中间加了一层：只是微温，也不太热心。

normal.en: Warmth is the noun; warmly is how a warm person acts.
normal.cn: warmth 是名词；warmly 是热情的人做事的方式。

abstract.en: Picture two cupped hands around a mug: the word is a small, safe heat you can hold.
abstract.cn: 想象双手捧住一只杯子：这个词是可以握住的、安全的小小热度。

abstract.en: The same rise in temperature serves both skin and feeling, so friendliness is spoken of as heat.
abstract.cn: 同一种温度上升同时服务于皮肤与情感，于是友善被说成热度。

abstract.en: Warmth is always comparative in practice: warm relative to the air, the room, or the person.
abstract.cn: 温暖在实践中总是相对的：相对于空气、房间或那个人。

examples.en: The stone wall stayed warm long after sunset.
examples.cn: 日落很久之后，那面石墙还是暖的。

examples.en: She warmed her hands over the small stove.
examples.cn: 她把手放在小炉子上取暖。

examples.en: The villagers gave the teachers a warm welcome.
examples.cn: 村民们热情地欢迎这些老师。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我母」——我母亲的手总是暖的：温暖的

root: 古英语 wearm「暖的」，源自日耳曼语同一词根，与德语 warm、荷兰语 warm 同源；派生词有 warmth、warmly、warmer。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of warm share one moderate heat: pleasant air, clothing that keeps it, a friendly manner, the act of adding heat, and finally the slow warming of affection.
sensesIntro.cn: warm 的五个义项共用同一种适中的热：宜人的空气、留热的衣物、亲切的态度、加热的动作，最后是感情慢慢变暖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two hands cupped around a mug of hot tea, fingers slowly coming back to life.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手捧住一杯热茶，指尖慢慢回温。

branches.en: AIR LINE: heat that feels good on the skin.
branches.cn: 空气线：皮肤上觉得舒服的热。

branches.en: CLOTHING LINE: heat held close to the body.
branches.cn: 衣物线：紧贴身体留住的热。

branches.en: FEELING LINE: friendliness, and its slow rising.
branches.cn: 情感线：亲切，以及它缓慢的升温。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: heat applied a little at a time.
branches.cn: 动作线：一点一点加上的热。

branches.en: CONTRAST: hot burns, warm comforts, lukewarm disappoints.
branches.cn: 对照线：hot 烫，warm 舒服，lukewarm 让人失望。

intro.en: Warm is a native Germanic word; the endings it takes are ordinary English suffixes.
intro.cn: warm 是本族日耳曼语词；它接的都是普通英语后缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 警告；提醒；告诫；预先通知
definition_en: to tell someone about a possible danger or problem so that they can avoid it
core_image: 一个人伸手拦住同伴，指着前方，要他在踏出下一步之前先停下
scene: 山路边的牌子被风吹得咣咣响，护林员在岔口拦住游客。He warned us that the path would be icy after dark.
sceneCN: 这里 warn 是「警告、提醒」（第 1 个义项：告知可能发生的危险，以便对方避开）；句意为他提醒我们天黑后小路会结冰。伸手拦住同伴的动作，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 动词：警告、告诫；提醒；预先通知

collocations.zh: 受到警告；要有心理准备

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「警告；警告信号」
由过去分词转形容词，义为「已受警告的」
加后缀 -er 构成，义为「警告者；报警装置」
加前缀 fore- 构成，义为「预先警告」

senses.title: To tell of danger
senses.definition: to tell someone about a danger or problem before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在危险或问题发生之前告诉某人
senses.example: The coastguard warned the boats about the coming storm.
senses.exampleCN: 海岸警卫队警告船只将有暴风雨来袭。
senses.why: Old English warnian meant to take heed and to admonish; the word names the act of making someone careful before harm arrives.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 warnian 意为留心与告诫；这个词指在伤害到来之前使人警醒的动作。

senses.title: To advise against
senses.definition: to advise someone strongly not to do something
senses.definitionCN: 强烈劝告某人不要做某事
senses.example: Doctors warn against taking the pills on an empty stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 医生告诫不要空腹服用这些药片。
senses.why: The same forward look is aimed at an action: the danger is what the doing would bring, so the advice is a prohibition.
senses.whyCN: 同样是对未来的注视，只是这次落在某个动作上：危险正是这个动作会带来的，所以劝告成了禁令。

senses.title: To give notice in advance
senses.titleCN: 预先通知：提前告知某事会来
senses.definition: to inform someone in advance that something is going to happen
senses.definitionCN: 提前告知某人某事即将发生
senses.example: Nobody warned me that the office would close early.
senses.exampleCN: 没有人提前告诉我办公室会提前关门。
senses.why: With danger taken out, only the timing remains: the word still speaks of a thing before it happens.
senses.whyCN: 把危险抽掉之后，只剩下时间关系：这个词说的仍是事情发生之前的那一句话。

senses.title: To caution officially
senses.titleCN: 正式警告：由权威出面告诫
senses.definition: to caution a person officially, especially about behaviour or breaking a rule
senses.definitionCN: 由官方或权威出面告诫某人，尤指其行为或违规
senses.example: The referee warned the player before showing the card.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判在出示牌之前先警告了这名球员。
senses.why: An authority repeats the hedge at the cliff edge in a formal voice, and the next step is a penalty.
senses.whyCN: 权威以正式的口吻重演崖边那道拦阻，而下一步就是处罚。

senses.title: To keep someone off
senses.titleCN: 警告离开：阻止某人靠近
senses.definition: in the phrase warn off, to tell someone to stay away from a place or a person
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 warn off，令某人远离某地或某人
senses.example: The farmer warned the walkers off the closed field.
senses.exampleCN: 农场主警告散步的人离开那片封闭的田地。
senses.why: Here the warning becomes a wall of words: the message is not what to watch but where not to stand.
senses.whyCN: 此时警告变成了一道用话砌成的墙：信息不是该注意什么，而是不该站在哪里。

intro.en: Warn comes from an Old English word for refusing or forbidding, and it is close kin to 'beware'.
intro.cn: warn 来自古英语中表示「拒绝、禁止」的词，与 beware 关系很近。

items.en: Warnian meant 'to take heed, be careful', and also 'to admonish or forbid'.
items.cn: warnian 意为「留心、当心」，也表示「告诫、禁止」。

items.en: The noun waru meant 'care, protection, guard', part of the same Germanic cluster.
items.cn: 名词 waru 意为「注意、保护、看守」，属于同一日耳曼词群。

items.en: German warnen 'to warn' and Dutch waarschuwen in part share this history.
items.cn: 德语 warnen 与荷兰语的部分说法共享这段历史。

items.en: The shorter form warn came from the infinitive warnian, and the beware sense drifted to the separate word beware.
items.cn: 较短形式 warn 出自不定式 warnian，而「当心」这一义则漂移到独立词 beware 上。

items.en: The present range runs from a shout at a cliff edge to a formal letter from a court.
items.cn: 现代用法从崖边的呼喊一直到法庭的正式函件。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words with the warn / war shape; the near-meaning group gathers ways of telling people about risk.
note.cn: 形近组收形状相近的 warn、war 类词；近义组收告知风险的多种说法。

entries.definition: A statement or sign that tells of danger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「警告；警示」，指告知危险的话语或标志。

entries.definition: To be careful of something; the old be-wary sense kept as its own word.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「当心」，把古老的「警觉」义保存为独立词。

entries.definition: The past participle of wear, meaning used or damaged; a homophone trap.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，是 wear 的过去分词，意为磨损的；与本词同音，是易混点。

entries.definition: To twist out of shape; an unrelated word of different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「翘曲、扭曲」，与本词只是形近，来源无关。

entries.definition: To tell someone to be ready for danger; often brief and urgent.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使警觉」，多用于简短紧急的提醒。

entries.definition: To tell someone to be careful, often in a gentler or official tone.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「告诫」，语气较轻或偏正式。

entries.definition: To state an intention to harm; the warning becomes hostile.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「威胁」，警告在此变成了敌意。

entries.definition: To give someone advice about what to do; warmer and less about danger.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「建议」，语气更和气，重点不在危险。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English warnian and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 warnian，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: Warn, not scold: the point is to stop something before it hurts.
normal.cn: warn 不是责骂：要点是在造成伤害之前拦住它。

normal.en: Warn of a thing, warn against an action: the preposition shows the target.
normal.cn: warn of 后接事物，warn against 后接动作：介词显示对象。

normal.en: Beware carries the old careful sense of warn away as its own word.
normal.cn: beware 把 warn 古老的「当心」义带走，成了独立词。

normal.en: A warning can be a word, a sign or a red light.
normal.cn: warning 可以是一句话、一块标志牌或一盏红灯。

normal.en: Worn is a homophone and means used up: do not mix the two.
normal.cn: worn 是同音词，意为磨旧的：不要混用。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a companion's chest at the edge of a cliff: the body stops first, the explanation comes after.
abstract.cn: 想象在崖边一只手按住同伴的胸口：身体先停下，解释随后才来。

abstract.en: The word faces forward in time: it only works if heard before the harm.
abstract.cn: 这个词朝向未来：只有在伤害之前被听见，它才起作用。

abstract.en: From a shout to a printed notice to a court letter, the same forward-looking alarm.
abstract.cn: 从一声呼喊到一张通告，再到一封法庭来函，是同一种前瞻性的警报。

examples.en: The guide warned us that the bridge might be unsafe.
examples.cn: 导游提醒我们那座桥可能不安全。

examples.en: Doctors warn against skipping breakfast every day.
examples.cn: 医生告诫不要每天都不吃早饭。

examples.en: A red light warns drivers when the crossing is busy.
examples.cn: 人行横道忙碌时，红灯会提醒司机。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「网」——路边拉了红色警示网，提醒你别再往前走：警告

root: 古英语 warnian「留心、告诫、禁止」，与 waru「注意、保护」同属一个日耳曼词群；beware 保存了其中「当心」的一支；派生词有 warning、forewarn。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of warn all face forward in time: danger ahead, an action to avoid, news in advance, official caution, and a call to keep away.
sensesIntro.cn: warn 的五个义项都朝向未来：前方的危险、要避开的动作、提前的通告、正式的告诫，以及令人远离的喝止。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand held out against a companion's chest at the edge of a cliff.
core.cn: 核心意象：崖边一只横在同伴胸前的手。

branches.en: DANGER LINE: the word points at what is coming.
branches.cn: 危险线：这个词指着即将到来的东西。

branches.en: ACTION LINE: the advice is aimed at what not to do.
branches.cn: 动作线：劝告落在不该做的事上。

branches.en: NOTICE LINE: the warning may be plain information in advance.
branches.cn: 通知线：警告也可能只是提前告知信息。

branches.en: AUTHORITY LINE: an official voice repeats the same caution.
branches.cn: 权威线：官方声音重复同样的告诫。

branches.en: DISTANCE LINE: warn off pushes the person away.
branches.cn: 距离线：warn off 把人推得更远。

intro.en: Warn is a native verb; its relatives in English are the endings it takes and the beware branch.
intro.cn: warn 是本族动词；它在英语中的亲属是所接的词尾以及 beware 这一分支。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.example: It belongs to the same cluster.
items.exampleCN: 它与本词同属一个词群。

definition_zh: 黄蜂；胡蜂（细腰、有蜇针的膜翅目昆虫）；纸巢蜂；寄生蜂；无花果小蜂；黄蜂腰（束腰）；脾气尖刻的人；蜂蜇式的刺痛
definition_en: a slender-waisted stinging insect of the order Hymenoptera, including social paper wasps and solitary parasitic kinds; also used of a thin waist or a sharp temper
core_image: 屋檐下倒悬一只灰白色的纸巢，一只细腰黄蜂停在巢口，翅膀收拢成一条窄线
scene: 屋檐下的纸巢边缘，一只细腰黄蜂收紧翅膀停住。A wasp settles on the rim of the paper nest under the eaves.
sceneCN: 这里 wasp 指「细腰、有蜇针的膜翅目昆虫」（第 1 个义项：黄蜂这种昆虫）；句意为一只黄蜂停在屋檐下纸巢的边缘。可辨识物件：倒悬的纸巢、六角巢房、细腰、收拢的翅膀。

pos.zh: 黄蜂；胡蜂；脾气尖刻的人；黄蜂腰

derivatives.zh: 似黄蜂的；脾气尖刻的

senses.title: A slender-waisted stinging insect
senses.titleCN: 黄蜂：细腰、带蜇针的昆虫
senses.definition: a stinging insect with a narrow waist between thorax and abdomen, usually banded in yellow and black
senses.definitionCN: 胸腹之间有细腰、常带黄黑条纹的蜇人昆虫
senses.example: A wasp settles on the rim of the paper nest under the eaves.
senses.exampleCN: 一只黄蜂停在屋檐下纸巢的边缘。
senses.why: The core sense rests on two visible marks: the pinched waist and the sting, which separate wasps from bees in ordinary speech.
senses.whyCN: 核心义靠两个可见特征站住：掐细的腰与蜇针，日常说法靠这两点把黄蜂与蜜蜂分开。

senses.title: A social paper-nest builder
senses.definition: a social wasp that chews wood fibre into a grey paper nest with hexagonal cells
senses.definitionCN: 把木纤维嚼成灰色纸巢、巢内有六角巢房的社会性黄蜂
senses.example: Paper wasps raise their brood in a comb hung from a single stalk.
senses.exampleCN: 纸巢蜂把幼虫养在由一根短柄悬挂的巢脾里。
senses.why: The paper nest is the clearest everyday sign of this sense, because the material looks like grey cardboard.
senses.whyCN: 纸巢是这一义最直观的标志，因为材料看上去就像灰色硬纸板。

senses.title: A solitary hunting wasp
senses.definition: a solitary wasp that hunts insects or spiders and stocks a nest cell with them for its larva
senses.definitionCN: 单独捕猎昆虫或蜘蛛、把猎物储进巢房供幼虫食用的黄蜂
senses.example: The digger wasp paralyses a caterpillar and drags it into a burrow.
senses.exampleCN: 掘土蜂把一条毛虫麻痹后拖进地穴。
senses.why: Many wasps are not social at all; the hunting habit, not the nest, defines this group.
senses.whyCN: 许多黄蜂根本不成群；界定这一组的是捕猎习性，而非巢。

senses.title: A parasitic wasp used in pest control
senses.titleCN: 用于害虫防治的寄生蜂
senses.definition: a small wasp that lays its eggs inside or on another insect, killing the host as the larva grows
senses.definitionCN: 把卵产在另一昆虫体内或体表、幼虫成长时杀死寄主的小型黄蜂
senses.example: Farmers release a parasitic wasp that targets aphids.
senses.exampleCN: 农民释放一种专门寄生蚜虫的寄生蜂。
senses.why: Agriculture turned the parasitic habit into a service, so the word now names a biological control agent.
senses.whyCN: 农业把寄生习性变成一项服务，这个词因此也指生物防治手段。

senses.title: A fig-pollinating wasp
senses.definition: a tiny wasp that enters a fig and both pollinates the flowers and lays its eggs there
senses.definitionCN: 进入无花果内部、既为花传粉又产卵的小型黄蜂
senses.example: Each fig species depends on its own pollinating wasp.
senses.exampleCN: 每一种无花果都依赖各自专属的传粉小蜂。
senses.why: This sense is a precise partnership: the insect's life cycle and the fruit's seed set are locked together.
senses.whyCN: 这一义是一种精确的共生：昆虫的生命周期与果实的结籽彼此锁定。

senses.title: A very thin waist
senses.definition: a waist so narrow that it looks pinched, named after the insect's body
senses.definitionCN: 细得像被掐住一样的腰，因这种昆虫的体形得名
senses.example: The dress was cut to give a wasp waist above a full skirt.
senses.exampleCN: 这条裙子裁成上收的黄蜂腰，下接宽裙摆。
senses.why: The metaphor works by shape alone: the insect's waist is the standard image of an exaggerated cinch.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻只靠形状成立：黄蜂的腰就是「勒得极细」的标准图像。

senses.title: A sharp-tongued person
senses.definition: a person whose remarks sting, described as waspish rather than bee-like
senses.definitionCN: 言语像蜇人一样刺痛别人的人，用「waspish」而非像蜜蜂那样形容
senses.example: Her waspish reply ended the argument at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她尖刻的回应立刻终止了争论。
senses.why: The sting supplies the metaphor: honey is sweet, but this insect only stings, so the adjective marks a biting manner.
senses.whyCN: 蜇针提供了比喻：蜜是甜的，而这种昆虫只会蜇人，形容词因此标出刺人的态度。

senses.title: A painful stinging encounter
senses.definition: the sting of a wasp treated as a memorable event, as in a wasp sting on the arm
senses.definitionCN: 把被黄蜂蜇到当作一件难忘的事，如手臂上的黄蜂蜇伤
senses.example: A wasp sting swelled his wrist for two days.
senses.exampleCN: 一处黄蜂蜇伤让他的手腕肿了两天。
senses.why: Here the insect name works as a modifier on the injury, a common pattern in medical and everyday description.
senses.whyCN: 此处昆虫名作伤情的修饰语，是医学与日常描述中常见的模式。

intro.en: Wasp comes from Old English wæsp, wæps, a Germanic word for the stinging insect. Latin vespa is a distant cousin in form and meaning but not the source of the English word.
intro.cn: wasp 来自古英语 wæsp、wæps，是日耳曼语中指这种蜇人昆虫的词。拉丁 vespa 在形义上都相近，却不是英语这个词的来源。

items.en: Old English wæsp and wæps both occur; the modern spelling settled on wasp, with the s and p kept in that order.
items.cn: 古英语中 wæsp 与 wæps 两种写法都出现；现代拼写定为 wasp，s 与 p 保持这一顺序。

items.en: Dutch wesp and German Wespe belong with the English word to a Germanic group, reconstructed as *wapsu or *wabswō; the exact shape is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 荷兰语 wesp、德语 Wespe 与英语词同属一个日耳曼词组，重构为 *wapsu 或 *wabswō；确切形式属重构。

items.en: Latin vespa 'wasp' and English wasp look alike and mean the same thing, but each descends through its own branch; the similarity reflects a shared older source, not borrowing.
items.cn: 拉丁 vespa「黄蜂」与英语 wasp 形似义同，却各自沿不同分支传下；相似反映更早的共同来源，而非借词。

items.en: A link to a root meaning 'weave' has been proposed because paper wasps build comb from chewed fibre; this remains a hypothesis about the older root.
items.cn: 有人因纸巢蜂用嚼碎的纤维筑巢，提出该词与意为「编织」的词根有关；这仍只是关于更早词根的假说。

items.en: From the seventeenth century waspish described a stinging manner of speech, and later the wasp waist named a tightly cinched shape.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起 waspish 形容刺人的说话方式，后来黄蜂腰又指勒得极细的体形。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one sets out words that share letters with wasp but have nothing to do with the insect; group two lists the stinging insects people confuse it with.
note.cn: 第一组列出与 wasp 共享字母、却与昆虫无关的词；第二组列出人们常与之混淆的蜇人昆虫。

entries.definition: A wisp is a thin strand of hair or smoke; the shared letters are pure coincidence.
entries.definitionCN: wisp 指一缕头发或烟；共享的字母纯属巧合。

entries.definition: Rasp means to scrape or speak harshly and has no insect sense at all.
entries.definitionCN: rasp 意为刮擦或声音刺耳，完全没有昆虫义。

entries.definition: Gasp is a breathing verb; only the final letters overlap.
entries.definitionCN: gasp 是呼吸动词，仅末尾字母相同。

entries.definition: Warp comes from a weaving term meaning to twist, a different root despite the near-identical sound.
entries.definitionCN: warp 来自织造术语，意为扭曲，读音几乎相同但词根不同。

entries.definition: A bee is a fuzzy pollen collector that makes honey; a wasp is smooth, hunts or parasitises and does not make honey.
entries.definitionCN: 蜜蜂毛茸、采集花粉并酿蜜；黄蜂体表光滑、捕猎或寄生，不酿蜜。

entries.definition: A hornet is a large social wasp, so it is a kind of wasp rather than a separate thing.
entries.definitionCN: 胡蜂是体大的社会性黄蜂，因此是黄蜂的一种，而非另一类。

entries.definition: Yellow jacket is the American name for a small aggressive social wasp that nests in the ground.
entries.definitionCN: yellow jacket 是美式说法，指体小、攻击性强、在地下筑巢的社会性黄蜂。

entries.definition: A bumblebee is a large hairy bee that pollinates; its sting is mild compared with a wasp's.
entries.definitionCN: 熊蜂是体大、多毛的传粉蜂，蜇痛远轻于黄蜂。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The Germanic root wæsp gives the noun, the plural wasps and the adjective waspish.
normal.cn: 日耳曼词根 wæsp 给出名词、复数 wasps 与形容词 waspish。

normal.en: The family runs wasp, waspish, waspishly, waspishness and waspie.
normal.cn: 词族包括 wasp、waspish、waspishly、waspishness 与 waspie。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: paper wasp, solitary wasp, wasp waist, wasp sting.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：纸巢蜂、独居黄蜂、黄蜂腰、黄蜂蜇伤。

normal.en: Latin vespa looks like the English word but is a separate branch, not its source.
normal.cn: 拉丁 vespa 形似英语词，却是另一支，并非其来源。

normal.en: The narrowed waist is the quickest way to tell a wasp from a bee.
normal.cn: 掐细的腰是区分黄蜂与蜜蜂最快的办法。

abstract.en: Picture a grey paper city hanging from one stalk, each cell a nursery.
abstract.cn: 想象一座灰纸做的城挂在单根细柄上，每个小格都是育儿室。

abstract.en: Picture a waist pulled so tight that the body looks divided in two.
abstract.cn: 想象腰被勒得极紧，身体看上去分成两截。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that leaves a red mark wherever it lands.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话落到哪里，就在哪里留下红痕。

examples.en: A single paper wasp can build a nest the size of a fist in one summer.
examples.cn: 一只纸巢蜂一个夏天就能造出拳头大的巢。

examples.en: The parasitic wasp lays one egg in each aphid, and the larva eats it from inside.
examples.cn: 寄生蜂在每只蚜虫体内产一枚卵，幼虫从内部把它吃掉。

examples.en: His waspish comment about the plan silenced the whole room.
examples.cn: 他对该方案尖刻的评论让全场沉默。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「wasp（瓦斯扑）」——带着刺、脾气像瓦斯一样冲的细腰虫 → 黄蜂

root: 古英语 wæsp / wæps「黄蜂」；与荷兰语 wesp、德语 Wespe 同出日耳曼语，重构形式 *wapsu / *wabswō（重构形式）。拉丁 vespa 属另一分支，非英语词来源；「编织」词根联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the insect's body to its nests, its hunting and parasitic habits, and then to human shapes and tempers that the sting supplies.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从昆虫的身体移到它的巢、捕猎与寄生习性，再转到蜇针所供给的人体形状与脾气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow-waisted body with a sting at the tip, hanging beside a grey paper comb.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具细腰的躯体，末端带蜇针，悬在灰色纸巢旁。

branches.en: BODY SHAPE: the pinched waist belongs to the insect and to the dress cut after it.
branches.cn: 体形：掐细的腰既属昆虫，也属仿它裁剪的衣裙。

branches.en: NEST AND STING: the paper comb and the injury are the two facts people meet first.
branches.cn: 巢与蜇：纸巢与伤处是人最先遇到的两件事。

branches.en: HUNTING WAYS: solitary hunters and parasitic kinds show how varied the family is.
branches.cn: 捕猎方式：独居猎手与寄生种类显示这一科的多样。

branches.en: FIG PARTNERSHIP: one fig, one wasp, a locked life cycle.
branches.cn: 无花果共生：一种果、一种蜂，生命周期彼此锁定。

branches.en: SHARP TONGUE: the sting becomes a metaphor for speech that wounds.
branches.cn: 尖刻的舌头：蜇针变成伤人言语的比喻。

intro.en: Wasp is a Germanic root with only a few English derivatives; the technical vocabulary around it is mostly formed from Latin and Greek elements.
intro.cn: wasp 是日耳曼词根，英语派生词很少；围绕它的技术词汇多由拉丁与希腊成分构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin vespa gives vespid and vespiary in zoology, but these are learned borrowings, not relatives of the English noun.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vespa 在动物学中衍生出 vespid 与 vespiary，但那是学术借词，并非英语名词的同族。

items.example: A wasp patrols the eaves each summer.
items.exampleCN: 每年夏天都有黄蜂在屋檐巡飞。

items.example: He answered in a waspish tone.
She remarked waspishly that the plan was late.
items.exampleCN: 她尖刻地说这个方案来晚了。

items.example: His waspishness cost him two friends.
items.exampleCN: 他的尖刻让他失去了两个朋友。

items.example: The jacket is cut with a wasp waist.
The dancer wore a waspie under the gown.
items.exampleCN: 舞者在长裙下穿了束腰。

items.meaning: a wasp that builds paper comb
items.example: A paper wasp founded her colony on the porch.
items.exampleCN: 一只纸巢蜂在门廊建起了群体。

items.meaning: a wasp that lives on a host
items.example: The parasitic wasp controls the moth population.
items.exampleCN: 寄生蜂控制着蛾的数量。

items.example: The wasp beetle's bands imitate a stinging insect.
items.exampleCN: 蜂形天牛的色带模仿蜇人的昆虫。

definition_zh: 水；水域；浇水；给…喝水
definition_en: the clear liquid that falls as rain and fills rivers and seas, and to pour it on plants or give it to animals
core_image: 一捧从井里舀起的水，指缝间淌下细细的水线
scene: 她每天清早提着桶去井边，回来时鞋上全湿了。The garden needs to be watered twice a week in summer.
sceneCN: 这里 water 是「水」（第 1 个义项：雨水、河海中那种清澈的液体）；句意为夏天花园需要每周浇两次水。从指缝间淌下的水线就是这个词给的画面。

derivatives.zh: 加 -y 构成，义为「含水的；稀薄的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「浇水；灌溉」
复合词，义为「防水的」
复合词，义为「水下的」

senses.title: The liquid we drink
senses.definition: the clear liquid that has no colour, taste or smell, and that all life needs
senses.definitionCN: 无色无味、一切生命都需要的清澈液体
senses.example: He drank a glass of water and sat down.
senses.exampleCN: 他喝了一杯水，然后坐下。
senses.why: The basic sense is the liquid itself, the one thing the word has meant for over a thousand years.
senses.whyCN: 基本义就是这种液体本身，一千多年来这个词一直指它。

senses.title: A sea, lake or river area
senses.definition: in the plural or with a modifier, an area of sea, lake or river
senses.definitionCN: 用复数或加修饰语，指海、湖或河的一片区域
senses.example: The boat drifted into shallow waters near the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 小船漂进了近岸的浅水区。
senses.why: Where the liquid lies in a body large enough to name, the plural waters marks out that area.
senses.whyCN: 当这种液体聚成足够大、值得命名的一片时，用复数 waters 指那片区域。

senses.title: To pour water on plants
senses.definition: to pour water on plants or soil so that they can grow
senses.definitionCN: 给植物或土壤浇水以助其生长
senses.example: She waters the herbs every morning before work.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天上班前给香草浇水。
senses.why: Making the noun do the work of a verb is the simplest step: to water is to give water.
senses.whyCN: 让名词直接充当动词是最简单的一步：water 就是给水。

senses.title: Of the eyes, to fill with tears
senses.definition: of the eyes, to fill with tears, often because of wind or onions
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛因风或洋葱等而充满泪水
senses.example: The smoke made his eyes water.
senses.exampleCN: 烟熏得他眼睛流泪。
senses.why: The eye filling with liquid is water appearing where it does not belong, so the verb describes that too.
senses.whyCN: 眼里盈满液体，就是水出现在了不该出现的地方，于是动词也兼指此事。

senses.title: To give animals a drink
senses.definition: to lead animals to drink or to give them water
senses.definitionCN: 把牲畜牵去饮水或给它们水喝
senses.example: He watered the horses before the long ride.
senses.exampleCN: 长途骑行之前他先给马饮了水。
senses.why: Farm work made this a fixed use early: to water stock is to supply the one thing they must have.
senses.whyCN: 农活很早就固定了这一用法：water 牲畜就是供给它们必不可少的那个东西。

intro.en: Water is one of the oldest words in English, with the same root in German Wasser and Dutch water.
intro.cn: water 是英语最古老的词之一，德语 Wasser 与荷兰语 water 都出自同一词根。

items.en: The word was wæter, and it already meant both the liquid and a body of it.
items.cn: 古英语中作 wæter，当时就已兼指这种液体和一片水域。

items.en: The Germanic stem wat- spread across the family, giving German Wasser and Dutch water.
items.cn: 日耳曼词干 wat- 遍布整个语族，产生德语 Wasser 与荷兰语 water。

items.en: The root behind it probably meant wet or flow, linking the word to the way the liquid moves.
items.cn: 其词根大概意为「湿的、流动的」，把词与这种液体的流动方式联系起来。

items.en: The form water established itself and the verb to water appeared beside the noun.
items.cn: water 这一形式确立，动词 to water 也随名词出现。

items.en: The word then joined in dozens of compounds, from waterfall to waterproof, and in idioms for trouble.
items.cn: 此后这个词参与了大量复合词（从 waterfall 到 waterproof），也进入表示困境的习语。

note.en: The first group gathers compounds and forms of water, the second the words for the liquid in other states and for nearby things.
note.cn: 第一组收 water 的复合词与词形，第二组收液体的其他状态词与相关词。

entries.definition: Third person singular and the plural noun.
entries.definitionCN: 第三人称单数，也是名词复数

entries.definition: Past tense and past participle.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式与过去分词

entries.definition: The adjective meaning full of water.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「含水的」

entries.definition: The -ing form and the noun for the job.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，也是表示浇水这一工作的名词

entries.definition: Anything that flows, water included.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指流动的液体

entries.definition: Water made solid by cold.
entries.definitionCN: 水遇冷结成的冰

entries.definition: Water turned to gas by heat.
entries.definitionCN: 水受热变成的蒸汽

entries.definition: Water falling from the clouds.
entries.definitionCN: 从云中落下的雨水

normalIntro.en: One old word for the liquid serves both as noun and as verb, and builds compounds by the dozen.
normalIntro.cn: 这个古老的液体名词既作名词也作动词，还能造出大量复合词。

normal.en: Water the plants: the noun is the verb.
normal.cn: water the plants：名词直接作动词。

normal.en: Waters means a stretch of sea or lake, not several liquids.
normal.cn: waters 指一片海或湖，而不是几种液体。

normal.en: In deep water means in trouble.
normal.cn: in deep water 意为陷入困境。

normal.en: Waterproof is water plus proof, able to keep it out.
normal.cn: waterproof 是 water 加 proof：能挡住水。

normal.en: Water becomes ice and steam: liquid, solid, gas.
normal.cn: 水可成冰也可成汽：液态、固态、气态。

abstract.en: Picture water slipping between your fingers.
abstract.cn: 想水从指缝间滑下。

abstract.en: Hear a hose spitting over flower beds.
abstract.cn: 听水管在花坛上洒水的声音。

abstract.en: Feel cold water up to the knees.
abstract.cn: 感受没到膝盖的冷水。

examples.en: The lake water was still and very cold.
examples.cn: 湖水静止，冰凉得很。

examples.en: Someone should water these flowers.
examples.cn: 得有人来浇一浇这些花。

examples.en: The company is in deep water over the deal.
examples.cn: 这家公司因这桩交易陷入困境。

root: 古英语 wæter，来自日耳曼词干 wat-（湿的、流动），与德语 Wasser 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The liquid comes first, then a stretch of it, then the verb of pouring and drinking, and finally the tear in the eye.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是这种液体，接着是一片水域，然后是浇水与饮水的动作，最后是眼中的泪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water running through open fingers.
core.cn: 核心意象：从张开的指缝间流过的水。

branches.en: The liquid branch: a glass after a meal.
branches.cn: 液体分支：饭后的一杯水。

branches.en: The waters branch: a boat in shallow waters.
branches.cn: 水域分支：浅水中的小船。

branches.en: The pouring branch: herbs watered at dawn.
branches.cn: 浇灌分支：清早浇过的香草。

branches.en: The eye branch: smoke that makes eyes water.
branches.cn: 眼睛分支：熏得流泪的烟。

branches.en: The stock branch: horses watered before the ride.
branches.cn: 牲畜分支：出发前饮过水的马。

intro.en: Water takes -y and -ing, -ed and -es, and serves as the first element of many compounds such as waterproof and underwater.
intro.cn: water 可加 -y、-ing、-ed、-es，并作为前项构成 waterproof、underwater 等大量复合词。

latinIntro.en: Water is one of the oldest Germanic words in English and has no Latin source, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: water 是英语中最古老的日耳曼词之一，没有拉丁语来源，故拉丁条目为空。

definition_zh: 防水的；不透水的；防水材料；使防水
definition_en: not letting water through, and to treat something so that water cannot pass
core_image: 雨衣上一颗水珠滚成一粒圆球，滑下去，衣面还是干的
scene: 山顶忽然下起雨，别人都在找地方躲，他把帽子一压，外套上全是滚落的水珠。Take a waterproof; the forecast is bad.
sceneCN: 这里 waterproof 是「防水的」（第 1 个义项：水透不过去）；句意为带件雨衣吧，预报说天气不好。雨衣上滚落的水珠就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ing 构成，义为「防水处理；防水材料」
过去分词作形容词，义为「做过防水处理的」
近义复合词，义为「抗水的」
近义复合词，义为「不透水的；严密的」

senses.title: Not letting water through
senses.definition: made or treated so that water cannot pass through
senses.definitionCN: 经过制作或处理，使水无法透过
senses.example: These boots are waterproof enough for crossing the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 这双靴子防水够好，可以蹚过小溪。
senses.why: Water plus proof, in the old sense of proof meaning «able to resist», gives exactly «no water gets through».
senses.whyCN: water 加上 proof（古义为「能抵御」），正好得出「水进不去」。

senses.title: A waterproof garment
senses.definition: a coat or other garment made of waterproof material, often called waterproofs in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 用防水材料制成的外套等，常用复数 waterproofs 指整套防水衣物
senses.example: Pack your waterproofs before you set off.
senses.exampleCN: 出发前把防水衣物装好。
senses.why: When the adjective is used so often with one kind of clothing, the adjective becomes the name of that clothing.
senses.whyCN: 当形容词常与某一类衣物连用时，形容词本身就变成了这类衣物的名字。

senses.title: To treat with a waterproof coating
senses.definition: to put a substance on something so that water cannot get in
senses.definitionCN: 在物体上涂敷物质，使水无法渗入
senses.example: They waterproofed the roof before the rainy season.
senses.exampleCN: 雨季之前他们给屋顶做了防水。
senses.why: Making an object waterproof is a job, so the adjective took a verb form: to waterproof something.
senses.whyCN: 让物体防水是一项工作，因此这个形容词也有了动词形式：to waterproof。

senses.title: Of things seen as roughly water-safe
senses.definition: in product labels, said of watches and phones that survive contact with water, though often not deep diving
senses.definitionCN: 在商品标识中形容手表、手机等不怕接触水，但通常并非深潜可用
senses.example: The watch is waterproof to fifty metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这只手表防水深度五十米。
senses.why: Labels need a short, strong word, so waterproof was stretched to cover everything from ink to watches, with a stated depth.
senses.whyCN: 标签需要一个简短有力的词，于是 waterproof 被扩展到从墨水到手表，再附上一个标注深度。

intro.en: Waterproof is an English compound of water and proof, where proof keeps its old sense of «able to resist».
intro.cn: waterproof 由 water 与 proof 合成的英语复合词，其中 proof 保留着「能抵御」的古义。

items.en: Proof comes from the Latin probare through Old French, and first meant the act of testing.
items.cn: proof 经古法语来自拉丁语 probare，最初指「检验」这一行为。

items.en: From testing, proof came to mean tried and found good, and then able to resist, as in fireproof.
items.cn: 由检验引申出「经过试验而可靠」，再引申为「能抵御」，如 fireproof。

items.en: Water and proof were joined in the eighteenth century to describe cloth that rain could not pass.
items.cn: 十八世纪 water 与 proof 合成一词，用来形容雨透不过的布料。

items.en: Vulcanised rubber and waxed cloth made waterproofing a trade, with its own craftsmen.
items.cn: 硫化橡胶与蜡布使防水处理成为一门有专门匠人的行业。

items.en: The word now labels watches, phones and mascara, always with an implied «how deep» or «how long».
items.cn: 如今这词标在手电、手机与睫毛膏上，总暗含「多深」或「多久」。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on waterproof and its near partners, the second the related -proof compounds and resistance words.
note.cn: 第一组收 waterproof 的派生与近邻词，第二组收同类 -proof 复合词与表示抵挡的词。

entries.definition: Plural noun and third person singular.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数与第三人称单数

entries.definition: Past tense and participle, also an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 过去式与分词，也可作形容词

entries.definition: The noun for the treatment itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指防水处理本身的名词

entries.definition: Closed so tightly that no water can enter at all.
entries.definitionCN: 密封到滴水不进

entries.definition: Resists water but is not fully proof against it.
entries.definitionCN: 抗水，但不完全防水

entries.definition: The garment most often called waterproof.
entries.definitionCN: 雨衣，最常被称作 waterproof 的衣物

entries.definition: The same -proof pattern, but against fire.
entries.definitionCN: 同样的 -proof 构法，只是防的是火

entries.definition: Not allowing liquid to pass, a formal word.
entries.definitionCN: 不透水的，较正式

normalIntro.en: Water plus proof: proof here is not evidence but resistance, as in fireproof and soundproof.
normalIntro.cn: water 加 proof：这里的 proof 不是「证据」而是「抵御」，正如 fireproof、soundproof。

normal.en: Proof means proof against, not proof of.
normal.cn: 这里的 proof 是「防住」，不是「证明」。

normal.en: Waterproof is total; water-resistant only resists.
normal.cn: waterproof 是全防，water-resistant 只是抗。

normal.en: Waterproofs as a plural noun means the rain clothes you pack.
normal.cn: 复数名词 waterproofs 指打包带的雨具。

normal.en: The verb keeps the same spelling: to waterproof a roof.
normal.cn: 动词拼写不变：to waterproof a roof。

normal.en: Watertight is stronger still: nothing gets in at all.
normal.cn: watertight 更强：一点都进不去。

abstract.en: Picture round drops rolling off a sleeve.
abstract.cn: 想圆滚滚的水珠从衣袖上滚下。

abstract.en: Hear rain drumming and nothing reaching your skin.
abstract.cn: 听雨点敲打，却一丝没透到身上。

abstract.en: See a label: waterproof to fifty metres.
abstract.cn: 想标签上写着：防水五十米。

examples.en: You will need a waterproof coat for the hills.
examples.cn: 上山你需要一件防水外套。

examples.en: The tent is waterproof but the seams are not.
examples.cn: 帐篷是防水的，但接缝不是。

examples.en: They waterproofed the boots before the trip.
examples.cn: 出发前他们给靴子做了防水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃特普鲁夫」——沃特普鲁夫站在雨里，衣服上的水珠一颗颗滚下去，里面却干得能摊开报纸。

root: water（水）+ proof（古义「能抵御」），为十八世纪英语复合词。

sensesIntro.en: The adjective comes first, then the garment it names, then the verb of treating something, and finally its use on product labels.
sensesIntro.cn: 先讲形容词，再讲它命名的衣物，然后是做处理的动词，最后是它在商品标签上的用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop beading up and rolling off a sleeve.
core.cn: 核心意象：在衣袖上聚成珠、滚下去的一滴水。

branches.en: The material branch: boots that cross a stream.
branches.cn: 材料分支：能蹚过小溪的靴子。

branches.en: The clothing branch: waterproofs packed for the trip.
branches.cn: 衣物分支：为出行打包的雨具。

branches.en: The treating branch: a roof sealed for the rains.
branches.cn: 处理分支：为雨季封好的屋顶。

branches.en: The label branch: a watch rated to fifty metres.
branches.cn: 标签分支：标称五十米的手表。

branches.en: The trade branch: waxed cloth and waterproofing craft.
branches.cn: 行业分支：蜡布与防水手艺。

intro.en: Waterproof joins two free words and then takes -s, -ed and -ing like any verb; -ial words such as impermeable are its formal relatives.
intro.cn: waterproof 由两个自由词合成，再像普通动词一样加 -s、-ed、-ing；impermeable 一类正式词是它的远亲。

latinIntro.en: The element proof entered English through Old French from Latin probare, to test, which is where its sense of resistance grew.
latinIntro.cn: 构件 proof 经古法语来自拉丁语 probare（检验），「抵御」之义正是在那里长出来的。

definition_zh: 蜡；蜂蜡；蜡状物；（月亮）渐圆；增大
definition_en: a soft yellowish substance made by bees or used for polishing, and also the act of growing larger, as the moon does
core_image: 一支蜡烛被点燃，火苗边上慢慢淌下一道温热的蜡泪
scene: 桌上那支旧蜡烛烧到一半，融化的蜡顺着铜盘边缘凝成一圈淡黄。By midnight the candle had melted into a pool of wax on the brass plate.
sceneCN: 这里 wax 是「蜡」（第 1 个义项：蜜蜂或工业制成的柔软黄色物质）；句意为到午夜时，蜡烛已经化成一摊蜡留在铜盘上。火苗边淌下的那一道蜡泪就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 蜡状的；蜡质的
蜡制的；苍白的
蜡像；蜡制品
蜂蜡

senses.title: The substance of candles
senses.definition: a soft pale substance that melts easily and is used for candles, polish and seals
senses.definitionCN: 一种柔软、颜色浅、容易熔化的物质，用来做蜡烛、上光剂与封蜡
senses.example: The wax from the candle ran down onto the brass plate.
senses.exampleCN: 蜡烛的蜡淌下来，落在铜盘上。
senses.why: The earliest sense in English is the material itself, taken from the substance bees build with.
senses.whyCN: 英语里最古老的意思是这种材料本身，取自蜜蜂筑巢所用的东西。

senses.title: The material bees build with
senses.definition: the substance that bees produce and use to build the cells of their hive
senses.definitionCN: 蜜蜂分泌并用它筑成蜂巢小格的那种物质
senses.example: The beekeeper scraped the wax off the frames and saved it for polish.
senses.exampleCN: 养蜂人把蜂蜡从框架上刮下来，留着做上光剂。
senses.why: Because honeycomb was the everyday source, the plain word first meant this animal product.
senses.whyCN: 由于蜂巢是日常来源，这个普通名词最初就指这种动物产物。

senses.title: A likeness made of wax
senses.definition: a figure of a person modelled in wax, as in a museum
senses.definitionCN: 用蜡塑成的人像，常见于蜡像馆
senses.example: Visitors queue to photograph the wax figures in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 参观者排队在大厅里给蜡像拍照。
senses.why: A material soft enough to model gave English a short way to name the imitation itself.
senses.whyCN: 一种软到可以塑形的材料，让英语有了指称仿制人像的简便说法。

senses.title: To grow larger, as the moon
senses.definition: of the moon, to show more of its lit face night after night
senses.definitionCN: 指月亮一夜夜露出更多被照亮的表面
senses.example: The moon will wax for another week before it is full.
senses.exampleCN: 月亮还会再圆上一个星期才到满月。
senses.why: This growth sense comes from a different Old English verb meaning to increase, which now shares the spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这一「增长」义来自另一个古英语动词，意为增多，如今与蜡共用拼写。

senses.title: To increase or grow stronger
senses.definition: to become larger, stronger or more intense, in literary or formal use
senses.definitionCN: 在书面或正式用法中指变大、变强或变得更为强烈
senses.example: Interest in the old songs waxed again after the film appeared.
senses.exampleCN: 电影上映之后，人们对那些老歌的兴趣再度高涨。
senses.why: From the moon the verb spreads to anything that steadily increases, and usually pairs with wane.
senses.whyCN: 从月亮出发，这个动词扩展到一切稳步增长的事物，且常与 wane 成对使用。

senses.title: To apply wax to a surface
senses.definition: to rub wax onto a surface in order to polish or protect it
senses.definitionCN: 把蜡擦到表面上，使其光亮或受到保护
senses.example: He waxed the wooden floor until it shone.
senses.exampleCN: 他把木地板打了蜡，直到它发亮。
senses.why: Once the noun named the stuff, the verb could simply mean putting it on things.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指称这种材料，动词就可以直接表示把它涂上去。

intro.en: Wax as a substance goes back to Old English weax, and the verb meaning to grow is a separate Old English word that later fell into the same spelling.
intro.cn: 表示物质的 wax 可上溯到古英语 weax；表示「增长」的动词则是另一个古英语词，后来拼写并入了一处。

items.en: Weax named the material of honeycomb, a word shared with the other old Germanic tongues.
items.cn: weax 指蜂巢的材料，这个词与其他古老日耳曼语言共有一个来源。

items.en: The Germanic root is related to words for weaving, since bees appear to weave their cells.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根与「编织」有关，因为在人看来蜜蜂像是在把巢房编出来。

items.en: A separate verb weaxan meant to grow or increase, and it described the moon as well as plants.
items.cn: 另有一个独立的动词 weaxan，意为生长、增多，既用于植物也用于月亮。

items.en: The two words came to be written alike, so wax meant both the substance and the growing.
items.cn: 两个词的写法逐渐趋同，于是 wax 同时表示材料与增长。

items.en: English kept the moon phrase wax and wane and added the everyday verb to wax a floor.
items.cn: 英语保留了 wax and wane 这一月亮短语，又添出「给地板打蜡」这样的日常动词。

note.en: The first group is built on the same material, the second on the idea of growing.
note.cn: 第一组来自同一种材料，第二组来自「增长」这一概念。

normalIntro.en: Hold the two lives of wax apart: one is a soft yellow material, the other is steady growth.
normalIntro.cn: 把 wax 的两副面孔分开记：一面是柔软的黄色材料，一面是稳步的增长。

normal.en: Wax on a candle melts; wax on a floor is rubbed in.
normal.cn: 蜡烛上的蜡会熔化，地板上的蜡是被擦进去的。

normal.en: Beeswax is the wax that bees make.
normal.cn: beeswax 就是蜜蜂做的那种蜡。

normal.en: Wax and wane is the moon pair; wax alone means to grow.
normal.cn: wax and wane 是月亮的一对，单独的 wax 意为增长。

normal.en: A wax figure is a person copied in wax.
normal.cn: wax figure 是用蜡复制出来的人。

normal.en: To wax a floor is to put the noun onto the floor.
normal.cn: wax a floor 就是把名词蜡涂到地板上。

abstract.en: Picture a flame leaning sideways as a drop slides down.
abstract.cn: 想火苗被压得歪一点，一滴蜡正往下滑。

abstract.en: Feel the floor turn smooth under the cloth.
abstract.cn: 感受地板在布下面变得光滑。

abstract.en: See a thin bright edge on the moon getting wider.
abstract.cn: 看月亮那道细细的亮边一点点变宽。

examples.en: The wax figures in the museum are replaced every few years.
examples.cn: 博物馆里的蜡像每隔几年就会更换。

examples.en: She waxed the old table until the grain stood out.
examples.cn: 她给旧桌子打了蜡，木纹清晰起来。

examples.en: Public anger waxed as the weeks passed.
examples.cn: 随着一周周过去，公众的愤怒越来越大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挖克斯」——挖克斯老头守着一支蜡烛，蜡一点点淌下来，月亮也一点点圆起来。

root: 古英语 weax（蜂蜡，与「编织」词根相关）+ 古英语 weaxan（生长、增多）；同源词有 waxy、beeswax。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as a material, spreads to things made of it, and is joined by an older verb of growing that the spelling swallowed.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初指一种材料，扩展到用它做成的东西，又并入了一个更古老的「生长」动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of soft yellow wax sliding down a candle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴柔软的黄色蜡顺着蜡烛滑落。

branches.en: The material branch: candles and the honeycomb it comes from.
branches.cn: 材料分支：蜡烛与它来源的蜂巢。

branches.en: The copy branch: figures modelled from the same stuff.
branches.cn: 仿制分支：用同一种材料塑出的人像。

branches.en: The growth branch: a moon filling out and anger rising.
branches.cn: 增长分支：月亮渐圆与怒气渐涨。

branches.en: The doing branch: rubbing the noun onto wood.
branches.cn: 动作分支：把名词蜡擦到木头上。

branches.en: The source branch: what the bees leave in the hive.
branches.cn: 来源分支：蜜蜂留在蜂巢里的东西。

intro.en: Wax is a native Germanic word, so the affixes here are mostly compounds and endings that grew in English.
intro.cn: wax 是本土日耳曼词，所以这里的构词主要是英语内部长出的复合与词尾。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin verb for wax, so the Latin table stands empty and only the native roots are shown.

definition_en: a road or route, and also the method, manner or direction in which something is done
