任性的；难以驾驭的

senses.title: A road or route
senses.definition: a path or road along which someone travels from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 供人从一处走到另一处的路径或道路
senses.example: He knows a short way across the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 他知道一条穿过田野的近路。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the road underfoot, from a Germanic word for road.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是脚下的路，来自一个表示道路的日耳曼词。

senses.title: A method of doing something
senses.definition: the method or manner used to achieve something
senses.definitionCN: 用来达成某事的做法或方式
senses.example: There must be a better way of solving this problem.
senses.exampleCN: 解决这个问题一定还有更好的办法。
senses.why: A road leads to a place, so the word easily shifted to whatever leads to a result.
senses.whyCN: 路把人带到某地，于是这个词顺理成章地指通向结果的任何做法。

senses.title: A manner or style
senses.definition: the manner in which something happens or is done
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生或进行时所呈现的样子
senses.example: She smiled in a way that made everyone relax.
senses.exampleCN: 她笑的样子让所有人都放松下来。
senses.why: From a method carried out to the shape of the carrying out itself is a very short step.
senses.whyCN: 从「做事的办法」到「做事的样子」，只差很小一步。

senses.title: Direction or side
senses.definition: the direction in which something faces or moves, or one of several sides
senses.definitionCN: 某物朝向或移动的方向，或若干侧面之一
senses.example: Which way does the wind blow in autumn?
senses.exampleCN: 秋天风往哪个方向吹？
senses.why: A road has two ends, so the word came to answer the question of which end one faces.
senses.whyCN: 路有两端，于是这个词也能回答朝向哪一端。

senses.title: Distance or a stretch of space
senses.definition: a distance, especially one measured as a stretch to be covered
senses.definitionCN: 一段距离，尤其指要走完的一段路
senses.example: The station is a good way from the hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 车站离旅馆有不短的一段路。
senses.why: The road sense measures itself: how much road lies between two places is a distance.
senses.whyCN: 道路义自身就可以度量：两地之间有多少路，就是多远。

senses.title: State or condition
senses.definition: the condition someone or something is in, usually in set phrases
senses.definitionCN: 人或事物所处的状况，多见于固定说法
senses.example: The firm is in a bad way after the floods.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水过后这家公司境况不佳。
senses.why: In older idiom a person could be said to stand in a way, and the road image turned into condition.
senses.whyCN: 在较老的习语里，人被说成处在某条路上，道路的意象就转成了境况。

senses.title: Very much, far
senses.definition: by a great amount, used informally with comparatives and prepositions
senses.definitionCN: 在口语中与比较级或介词连用，表示程度很大
senses.example: The new bridge is way longer than the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 新桥比旧桥长得多。
senses.why: This emphatic use grew out of the distance sense in American speech.
senses.whyCN: 这一强调用法由「距离」义在美式口语中生长出来。

intro.en: Way is a native Germanic word for a road, recorded in Old English as weg, and it has kept that concrete core for well over a thousand years.
intro.cn: way 是本土日耳曼语的道路词，古英语写作 weg，一千多年来一直保留着这个具体的核心。

items.en: The Germanic root meant to carry or to move, and the noun named the line along which things move.
items.cn: 这一日耳曼词根意为搬运、移动，名词便指事物移动所沿的那条线。

items.en: Weg meant road, path and also journey, and it appears in the oldest English poetry.
items.cn: weg 意为道路、小径，也指旅程，出现在最古老英语诗歌里。

items.en: Spelling settled as way, and the word began to cover manner as well as road.
items.cn: 拼写定为 way，这个词开始既指道路也指方式。

items.en: Compounds such as highway and railway made the road sense part of daily travel.
items.cn: highway、railway 这类复合词让道路义进入了日常出行。

items.en: American speech added the emphatic use in such phrases as way better.
items.cn: 美式口语又添出 way better 之类的强调用法。

note.en: The first group are compounds and relatives of the road word, the second the words it stands beside most often.
note.cn: 第一组是道路词的复合与亲属词，第二组是它最常并列的词。

entries.definition: A main road between towns.
entries.definitionCN: 公路；干道

entries.definition: A track on which trains run.
entries.definitionCN: 铁路

entries.definition: An underground railway in a city.
entries.definitionCN: 城市地铁

entries.definition: The opening where a door stands.
entries.definitionCN: 门口；门道

entries.definition: A prepared surface for vehicles, the physical road.
entries.definitionCN: 道路；马路

entries.definition: The line chosen from one place to another.
entries.definitionCN: 路线；航线

entries.definition: An organised way of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 方法；办法

entries.definition: The way in which something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 方式；举止

normalIntro.en: One short word covers road, method and manner because all three answer how one gets there.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短词同时覆盖道路、方法与方式，因为三者都在回答「怎么到达」。

normal.en: On the way means on the road, in the middle of a journey.
normal.cn: on the way 是在路上，在旅程中间。

normal.en: A way of doing something is the road that leads to the result.
normal.cn: a way of doing something 是通往结果的那条路。

normal.en: In a way softens a statement to one side of the truth.
normal.cn: in a way 把话软化为真相的一个侧面。

normal.en: Which way asks for direction, not method.
normal.cn: which way 问的是方向，不是方法。

normal.en: Way better is spoken English for much better.
normal.cn: way better 是口语里的 much better。

abstract.en: Picture a footpath polished by shoes.
abstract.cn: 想一条被鞋底磨亮的小路。

abstract.en: Follow the line of the path with your eyes until it bends.
abstract.cn: 用眼睛沿着路走，直到它拐弯。

abstract.en: Feel two choices as two branches of the same road.
abstract.cn: 把两个选择感受成同一条路的分岔。

examples.en: Could you show me the way to the station?
examples.cn: 你能告诉我去车站的路吗？

examples.en: That is one way to save money, but not the safest.
examples.cn: 那是一种省钱的方法，但不是最稳妥的。

examples.en: The box was way too heavy for one person.
examples.cn: 这个箱子一个人搬实在太重了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂」——在路口喊一声「喂」，问的既是路，也是走法。

root: 日耳曼语词根（搬运、移动）→ 古英语 weg（道路、旅程）→ 中古英语 way；同源词有 highway、railway、wayward。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts under the feet as a road, then answers how, then where, then how far, then how things stand, and finally how much.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从脚下的路出发，继而回答怎么做、朝哪里、有多远、处境如何，最后是程度有多深。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow footpath worn bright by walking.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条被人走亮的小径。

branches.en: The road branch: a short cut across the fields.
branches.cn: 道路分支：穿过田野的近路。

branches.en: The method branch: how a problem is solved and how a smile looks.
branches.cn: 方法分支：问题怎么解、笑容是什么样子。

branches.en: The space branch: which direction and how far.
branches.cn: 空间分支：朝哪个方向、有多远。

branches.en: The state branch: a firm in a bad way.
branches.cn: 状态分支：境况不佳的公司。

branches.en: The degree branch: spoken way better.
branches.cn: 程度分支：口语里的 way better。

intro.en: Way works as the second half of many compounds, so its main affix life is as a combining form.
intro.cn: way 常作许多复合词的后半，所以它的主要构词生活是作为组合形式。

latinIntro.en: Way is a Germanic word with no Latin source, so the Latin table is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: way 是日耳曼词，没有拉丁来源，故拉丁表留空。

definition_zh: 减弱；削弱；使变弱；变弱
definition_en: to make someone or something less strong, or to become less strong
core_image: 一根木梁上一道裂缝慢慢变宽，撑不住屋顶了
scene: 洪水退去后，桥墩上留下一道细缝，几个月后那道缝已经宽得能插进手指。Flood water had weakened the bridge pier until the crack widened.
sceneCN: 这里 weaken 是「削弱」（第 1 个义项：使某物力量变小）；句意为洪水把桥墩削弱了，裂缝越变越宽。那道慢慢变宽、撑不住屋顶的裂缝就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 弱的；虚弱的
虚弱；弱点
削弱者；削弱物
减弱；削弱
未被削弱的

senses.title: To make something less strong
senses.definition: to reduce the strength, force or solidity of something
senses.definitionCN: 降低某物的力量、强度或坚固程度
senses.example: Repeated flooding weakened the bridge pier.
senses.exampleCN: 反复的洪水削弱了桥墩。
senses.why: The verb simply turns the adjective into an action: to give weakness to something.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把形容词变成动作：把弱加给某物。

senses.title: To become less strong
senses.definition: to lose strength or force without an outside agent
senses.definitionCN: 在没有外力作用下失去力量或强度
senses.example: His voice weakened as the evening went on.
senses.exampleCN: 夜渐深，他的声音越来越弱。
senses.why: English -en verbs work both ways, so weaken can act alone as well as on an object.
senses.whyCN: 英语的 -en 动词可及物也可不及物，故 weaken 既能带宾语也能单独使用。

senses.title: To reduce power or influence
senses.definition: to make a person, group or institution less powerful or effective
senses.definitionCN: 使人、团体或机构的力量或效能变小
senses.example: The scandal weakened the minister’s position in the party.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩丑闻削弱了这位部长在党内的地位。
senses.why: Power and influence are kinds of strength, so a loss of them is weakening too.
senses.whyCN: 权力与影响力也是某种力量，失去它们同样是「被削弱」。

senses.title: To make an argument or case less convincing
senses.definition: to make a claim, excuse or argument less persuasive
senses.definitionCN: 使主张、借口或论据不那么有说服力
senses.example: One false date weakens the whole report.
senses.exampleCN: 一个错误的日期就能让整份报告站不住脚。
senses.why: Influence and credibility are kinds of strength, so loss of them is also weakening.
senses.whyCN: 影响力与可信度都是某种力量，失去它们同样是「变弱」。

senses.title: To become less intense or less firm
senses.definition: of a feeling or determination, to become less firm
senses.definitionCN: 指情绪或决心变得不那么坚定
senses.example: She refused at first, but her resolve weakened at the last minute.
senses.exampleCN: 她起初拒绝了，但最后一刻决心动摇了。
senses.why: Determination is felt as a force that holds firm, and it thins the way a rope does.
senses.whyCN: 决心被感受为一股撑住不倒的力量，会像绳子那样变松变细。

intro.en: Weaken is an English verb made from weak plus the suffix -en, the same pattern as deepen and widen.
intro.cn: weaken 是由 weak 加后缀 -en 构成的英语动词，与 deepen、widen 属于同一模式。

items.en: The adjective weak came into English from veikr, a Norse word for giving way.
items.cn: 形容词 weak 从意为退让的诺斯词 veikr 进入英语。

items.en: Once weak was in everyday use, speakers began to make a verb of it with the native -en ending.
items.cn: weak 进入日常用法后，人们开始用本土词尾 -en 把它变成动词。

items.en: Weaken appeared beside similar pairs such as hard and harden, wide and widen.
items.cn: weaken 与 hard、harden，wide、widen 这类成对形式并列出现。

items.en: The verb is used of bodies, structures, currencies and arguments alike.
items.cn: 这个动词既用于身体、结构，也用于货币与论据。

items.en: The participle weakened is common in the passive, as in weakened by years of neglect.
items.cn: 过去分词 weakened 在被动语态中很常见，如「因长年失修而受损」。

note.en: The first group is the weak family itself, the second the verbs that do similar work.
note.cn: 第一组是 weak 词族本身，第二组是做类似工作的动词。

entries.definition: Not strong in body, force or quality.
entries.definitionCN: 弱的；虚弱的

entries.definition: The state of being weak, or a failing.
entries.definitionCN: 虚弱；弱点

entries.definition: Something that makes another thing weaker.
entries.definitionCN: 削弱者；削弱物

entries.definition: Less strong than another.
entries.definitionCN: 更弱的

entries.definition: To weaken something gradually from below.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐削弱；暗中破坏

entries.definition: To damage a faculty or function.
entries.definitionCN: 损害；削弱（功能）

entries.definition: To make or become smaller.
entries.definitionCN: 减少；减小

entries.definition: To weaken something by adding water or another element.
entries.definitionCN: 稀释；削弱

normalIntro.en: Weaken is the simplest way English turns an adjective into a verb: add -en and the quality becomes a change.
normalIntro.cn: weaken 是英语把形容词变动词的最简单办法：加 -en，性质就变成变化。

normal.en: Weak is what something is; weaken is what happens to it.
normal.cn: weak 是事物是什么样，weaken 是它遭遇了什么。

normal.en: Deepen, widen, harden, weaken all use the same -en.
normal.cn: deepen、widen、harden、weaken 都用同一个 -en。

normal.en: You can weaken a bridge, a case or a currency.
normal.cn: 桥、论据、货币都可以被削弱。

normal.en: The passive weakened by illness is very common.
normal.cn: 被动式 weakened by illness 很常见。

normal.en: Weakening is also the noun, as in a weakening of demand.
normal.cn: weakening 也是名词，如需求减弱。

abstract.en: Watch a hairline crack open wider each winter.
abstract.cn: 想一道细缝在每个冬天都裂得更宽。

abstract.en: Feel a grip loosen one finger at a time.
abstract.cn: 感受一次握手一根手指一根手指地松开。

abstract.en: Hear a drumbeat that slowly loses its force.
abstract.cn: 听鼓点一点点失去力道。

examples.en: Years of rain have weakened the stone wall.
examples.cn: 多年的雨水侵蚀使这堵石墙变弱了。

examples.en: The illness left him weakened for a whole month.
examples.cn: 这场病让他虚弱了整整一个月。

examples.en: Such excuses only weaken your case.
examples.cn: 这样的借口只会让你的论点站不住脚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威肯」——威肯工程师发现桥墩有缝，赶紧报告：这些裂缝正在削弱桥体。

root: 古诺斯语 veikr（易弯、退让）→ weak；加英语后缀 -en 构成动词 weaken，与 deepen、widen 同类。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with a structure losing solidity, then widens to power, arguments and finally to determination.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从结构失去坚固出发，再扩展到权力、论据，最后是决心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crack in a beam opening wider.
core.cn: 核心意象：梁上的一道裂缝越变越宽。

branches.en: The structural branch: flood water and a bridge pier.
branches.cn: 结构分支：洪水与桥墩。

branches.en: The self-acting branch: a voice fading at night.
branches.cn: 自变分支：夜里逐渐弱下去的声音。

branches.en: The power branch: a minister’s position damaged.
branches.cn: 权力分支：受损的部长地位。

branches.en: The argument branch: one wrong date spoils a report.
branches.cn: 论据分支：一个错误日期毁掉报告。

branches.en: The will branch: resolve that gives way late.
branches.cn: 意志分支：最后一刻动摇的决心。

intro.en: Weaken is a native derivation: an adjective from Old Norse plus the English suffix -en.
intro.cn: weaken 是本土派生：一个来自古诺斯语的形容词加上英语后缀 -en。

latinIntro.en: Neither part is Latin, so the Latin table only records the Norse adjective behind weak.
latinIntro.cn: 两部分都不来自拉丁语，故拉丁表只记 weak 背后的诺斯形容词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into a verb.

definition_zh: 虚弱；弱点、缺陷；（对某事物的）偏爱、迷恋
definition_en: lack of strength, a fault in a person or thing, or a strong liking that is hard to resist
core_image: 一根细绳被拉得发紧，中间已经有了磨白的痕迹
scene: 老木桥的栏杆被人一靠就晃，木板缝里透出下面的河。The weakness of the old bridge was obvious to anyone who looked closely.
sceneCN: 这里 weakness 是「弱点、缺陷」（第 2 个义项：人或事物不够牢固的地方）；句意为任何人只要看仔细些，都能发现这座老桥的弱点。磨白的绳痕，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：虚弱、无力；弱点、缺陷；偏爱

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根形容词，义为「虚弱的；薄弱的」
加动词后缀 -en 构成，义为「削弱；变弱」
加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「虚弱地；无力地」
由 weak 加 -ing 构成，义为「体弱者」（口语罕用）

senses.title: Lack of physical strength
senses.definition: the state of lacking physical strength or energy
senses.definitionCN: 缺少体力或精力的状态
senses.example: After the fever, a deep weakness stayed in his legs for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 退烧之后，他双腿的虚弱感持续了好几周。
senses.why: The suffix -ness turns an adjective into a state; weakness is simply the state of being weak.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ness 把形容词变成状态；weakness 就是「弱」这一状态。

senses.title: A fault in a person
senses.definition: a fault or defect in someone's character, such as impatience or pride
senses.definitionCN: 某人性格中的欠缺，如急躁或自负
senses.example: His one real weakness is that he cannot say no to a friend.
senses.exampleCN: 他唯一真正的弱点是无法拒绝朋友的请求。
senses.why: The adjective weak names a lack of strength; -ness turns that lack into a countable fault, one particular place where the strength runs out.
senses.whyCN: 形容词 weak 表示力量不足；后缀 -ness 把这种不足变成可数的缺点，即力量耗尽的某一处。

senses.title: A weak point in a thing
senses.titleCN: 缺陷：事物中不牢固的地方
senses.definition: a part of a system, structure or argument that is not strong or convincing
senses.definitionCN: 系统、结构或论证中不够牢固、不够有说服力的部分
senses.example: Engineers found a weakness where the two beams meet.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师发现两根梁相接之处的薄弱点。
senses.why: The same noun moves from people to things: any structure is judged by its least strong part.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词从人移到物：任何结构都以最不牢固的部分来评判。

senses.title: A strong liking
senses.definition: a strong liking for something that one finds hard to resist
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物强烈而难以抗拒的喜爱
senses.example: She has a weakness for old watches.
senses.exampleCN: 她对旧手表有一种偏爱。
senses.why: Here the fault turns inward and pleasant: a liking you cannot resist is a weak spot in your self-control.
senses.whyCN: 这里缺陷转向内里且变得愉快：抵挡不住的喜爱，正是自制力上的薄弱处。

senses.title: Lack of force or authority
senses.titleCN: 软弱无力：力量或权威不足
senses.definition: lack of strength in a government, argument or action, so that it has little effect
senses.definitionCN: 政府、论证或行动缺乏力度，因而收效甚微
senses.example: The weakness of the new law was clear from the first month.
senses.exampleCN: 新法的软弱无力在头一个月就显露出来。
senses.why: Weakness of a law or a case means it cannot stand up to challenge, the same image of strength running out.
senses.whyCN: 法律或论证的软弱，指它经不起挑战，仍是力量耗尽的同一意象。

intro.en: Weakness is a native English compound of the old adjective weak and the noun suffix -ness.
intro.cn: weakness 是本族英语复合词，由古老形容词 weak 与名词后缀 -ness 组成。

items.en: The adjective veikr meant 'pliant, weak'; it entered English from Norse rather than from Old English.
items.cn: 形容词 veikr 意为「柔软的、弱的」，是从古诺尔斯语而非古英语进入英语的。

items.en: Old English had its own wac, meaning 'weak, pliant', related to the verb wican 'to give way'.
items.cn: 古英语自有 wac，意为「弱的、柔软的」，与动词 wican「退让」相关。

items.en: The two forms merged into the single adjective weik or weak in the north of England first.
items.cn: 两种形式合并为单一形容词，先在英格兰北部写成 weik 或 weak。

items.en: The suffix -nesse was fully productive, so weakness appeared as soon as the adjective was established.
items.cn: 后缀 -nesse 当时构词能力很强，形容词一成形，weakness 便随之出现。

items.en: The figurative senses, a fault and a fondness, are later extensions of the same state.
items.cn: 「缺陷」与「迷恋」两个比喻义，是同一种状态后来伸出的延伸。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the weak family; the near-meaning group gathers words for faults and for fondness.
note.cn: 形近组收 weak 一族词；近义组收表示缺陷与偏爱的说法。

entries.definition: The adjective for lacking strength; the base of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「虚弱的」，是名词的词根。

entries.definition: To make or become weaker.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「削弱；变弱」。

entries.definition: In a weak way; also an old adjective meaning sickly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「虚弱地」；也曾是表示「病弱的」形容词。

entries.definition: Seven days; a homophone with no connection in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「星期」，与本词同音，来源无关。

entries.definition: A small fault that spoils something; sharper and more specific.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「瑕疵、缺陷」，更尖锐也更具体。

entries.definition: A mistake or a defect for which someone can be blamed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「过错、缺点」，含可归咎之意。

entries.definition: Weakness of body or character, especially in old age.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「脆弱」，多指年老体弱或性格弱点。

entries.definition: A minor weakness in a person's character.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「缺点」，多指性格上的小毛病。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old Norse veikr and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古诺尔斯语 veikr，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: weak plus -ness: the suffix simply names the state, so weakness is the state of being weak.
normal.cn: weak 加 -ness：后缀只是给状态命名，weakness 就是「弱」的状态。

normal.en: Strengths and weaknesses always come in pairs: an honest list has both.
normal.cn: 长处与短处总是成对出现：诚实的清单上两样都有。

normal.en: A weakness for chocolate is not a defect but a fondness.
normal.cn: a weakness for chocolate 不是缺陷，而是一种偏爱。

normal.en: Weakness in an argument is a gap where evidence should be.
normal.cn: 论证中的 weakness 就是本该有证据的空缺。

normal.en: Week is a homophone and means seven days; weakness means no strength.
normal.cn: week 同音，指七天；weakness 指没有力气。

abstract.en: Picture a rope worn pale in the middle: the weak point is where the strain shows first.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳子中间磨得发白：弱点就是拉力最先显形的地方。

abstract.en: The word works for bodies, buildings, arguments and hearts, because all can give way under pressure.
abstract.cn: 这个词适用于身体、建筑、论证和人心，因为它们在压力下都可能让步。

abstract.en: Finding a weakness is not an insult; it is where a repair or a defence belongs.
abstract.cn: 找到弱点并不是侮辱，那正是修补或防守该落脚的地方。

examples.en: Weakness in the knees made the climb dangerous.
examples.cn: 膝盖无力让这次攀登变得危险。

examples.en: Every plan has a weakness, and this one is the budget.
examples.cn: 每个计划都有薄弱处，这个计划的薄弱处就是预算。

examples.en: He has a weakness for cheap second-hand books.
examples.cn: 他对便宜的二手书有种偏爱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「唯一（wei）克（k）尼斯（ness）」——唯一被克制的尼斯湖怪，因为太虚弱：虚弱

root: 由古诺尔斯语 veikr「柔软的、弱的」与古英语 wac 合流而成的 weak，加名词后缀 -ness 构成；同族词有 weaken、weakly、weakling。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of weakness begin with the plain state of no strength, then name a fault in a person, a gap in a thing, a fondness, and a general lack of force.
sensesIntro.cn: weakness 的五个义项始于「没有力气」这一朴素状态，继而指人的缺点、事物的空隙、一种偏爱，以及普遍的力量不足。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope worn pale in the middle where the strain shows first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根中间磨得发白的绳子，拉力最先在那里显形。

branches.en: BODY LINE: the muscles have no force left.
branches.cn: 身体线：肌肉再也使不出力。

branches.en: CHARACTER LINE: a person cannot resist a certain impulse.
branches.cn: 性格线：人抗拒不了某种冲动。

branches.en: STRUCTURE LINE: a beam, a law or an argument lacks force.
branches.cn: 结构线：梁、法条或论证缺乏力度。

branches.en: DESIRE LINE: the same word turns kind, naming a fondness.
branches.cn: 欲望线：同一个词转得温柔，指一种偏爱。

branches.en: CONTRAST: flaw is sharper, failing is gentler, weakness is the plainest.
branches.cn: 对照线：flaw 更尖锐，failing 更温和，weakness 最朴素。

intro.en: Weakness is a Germanic adjective plus the native -ness suffix; no Latin element is involved.
intro.cn: weakness 是日耳曼语形容词加本族的 -ness 后缀，不涉及拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

items.example: It merged with the Norse form.
items.exampleCN: 它与诺尔斯语形式合流。

items.example: It is the old verb behind wac.
items.exampleCN: 它是 wac 背后的古老动词。

definition_zh: 财富；财产；大量；丰富
definition_en: a large amount of money, property or valuable things, and also a great supply of anything good
core_image: 一只旧木箱打开了盖子，里面铜器、地契和金币挤得满满当当
scene: 祖屋搬迁时，家人在阁楼找到一只落满灰的木箱，里面塞着旧账本、银勺和成叠的地契。The old chest in the attic held the family’s wealth: ledgers, silver spoons and deeds.
sceneCN: 这里 wealth 是「财富」（第 1 个义项：钱财、财产等有价值的积累）；句意为阁楼里那只旧箱子里装着全家的财富。塞满铜器、银勺与地契的木箱就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 富有的；富裕的
富裕；富足
财产税；财富税
极其富有的
联邦；共同体

senses.title: Money and property
senses.definition: a large amount of money, land or other property owned by a person or group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或团体拥有的大量钱财、土地或其他财产
senses.example: The family’s wealth came from the wool trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这家的财富来自羊毛贸易。
senses.why: This is the economic core of the word: things that can be owned and counted.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词的经济核心：可被拥有、可被计数的东西。

senses.title: The state of being rich
senses.definition: the condition of having plenty of money or resources
senses.definitionCN: 拥有充足钱财或资源的状态
senses.example: He rose from poverty to wealth in a single decade.
senses.exampleCN: 他在一个十年里从贫穷走向富裕。
senses.why: From the thing owned the word shifts to the situation of owning plenty.
senses.whyCN: 从被拥有的东西，词义转向拥有大量的那种处境。

senses.title: A great amount of something good
senses.definition: a large supply of something valuable or useful, often abstract
senses.definitionCN: 某种有价值或有用之物的大量供给，常为抽象之物
senses.example: The library offers a wealth of material on local history.
senses.exampleCN: 这家图书馆提供大量本地史料。
senses.why: Anything plentiful is treated as treasure, so the word spreads beyond money.
senses.whyCN: 凡是充裕之物都被当作财宝，于是这个词走出了金钱的范围。

senses.title: Things of value in a wider sense
senses.definition: the total of valuable resources held by a place, such as minerals, forests or talent
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区所拥有的全部宝贵资源，如矿产、森林或人才
senses.example: The country’s greatest wealth is its trained teachers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家最大的财富是受过训练的教师。
senses.why: Skill and learning are treated as treasure that a place owns.
senses.whyCN: 技能与学识被当作一个地方所拥有的财宝。

senses.title: A good of the community
senses.definition: in older use, the general good or welfare of a community
senses.definitionCN: 较老的用法中指共同体的总体福祉
senses.example: The old prayer asked for the wealth of the whole town.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇古老的祈祷文祈求全镇的福祉。
senses.why: The earliest sense was well-being, and welfare is its close cousin in form and meaning.
senses.whyCN: 最早的意思是安康，welfare 在形式与意义上都是它的近亲。

intro.en: Wealth began as a word for well-being rather than money, built on the old adjective weal, meaning in good condition.
intro.cn: wealth 最初指安康而非钱财，由意为「状况良好」的古形容词 weal 构成。

items.en: Wela meant well-being and prosperity, and the derived noun described a state of good fortune.
items.cn: wela 意为安康与兴旺，其派生名词描述的是一种好运状态。

items.en: Wealthe appeared with the abstract ending -th, as in health and strength, meaning the condition of being well off.
items.cn: wealthe 带抽象词尾 -th 出现，如 health、strength，意为「境况良好」。

items.en: As trade grew the word shifted from a condition to the goods that produced it.
items.cn: 随着贸易发展，词义从一种状态转向产生这种状态的财物。

items.en: By the sixteenth century wealth plainly meant riches, and welfare took over the older sense.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，wealth 已明确指财富，旧义由 welfare 承接。

items.en: A wealth of followed, letting the word measure any abundance.
items.cn: a wealth of 随之出现，使这个词可以度量任何充裕之物。

note.en: The first group is the wealth family, the second the nouns that compete with it.
note.cn: 第一组是 wealth 词族，第二组是与它竞争的近义名词。

entries.definition: Having plenty of money or property.
entries.definitionCN: 富有的；富裕的

entries.definition: The same -th ending, but of the body.
entries.definitionCN: 健康

entries.definition: Well-being, the older sense of wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 福利；福祉

entries.definition: A political community or union of states.
entries.definitionCN: 联邦；共同体

entries.definition: Large amounts of money and valuable things.
entries.definitionCN: 财富；财宝

entries.definition: A very large amount of money, often inherited.
entries.definitionCN: 大笔财产

entries.definition: Things owned, especially land and buildings.
entries.definitionCN: 财产；房产

entries.definition: A very large quantity of something.
entries.definitionCN: 充裕；大量

normalIntro.en: Remember the old sense first: wealth once meant being well, and money was only how that well-being looked.
normalIntro.cn: 先记住旧义：wealth 原本指过得好，钱财只是这种「好」的外表。

normal.en: Weal means well-being, and -th makes it a state, as in health.
normal.cn: weal 是安康，-th 使它成为状态，正如 health。

normal.en: Welfare keeps the old sense; wealth keeps the goods.
normal.cn: welfare 保留了旧义，wealth 保留了财物。

normal.en: A wealth of information is a treasure of facts.
normal.cn: a wealth of information 就是事实的宝藏。

normal.en: Wealth is uncountable when it means riches.
normal.cn: 表示财富时不可数。

normal.en: The adjective is wealthy, not wealth.
normal.cn: 形容词是 wealthy，而不是 wealth。

abstract.en: Picture a chest crammed to the lid.
abstract.cn: 想一只塞到盖子的木箱。

abstract.en: Hear coins slide against old paper deeds.
abstract.cn: 听铜币在旧地契上滑动的声音。

abstract.en: Feel how much a single word can hold.
abstract.cn: 感受一个词能装下多少东西。

examples.en: The country’s wealth is unevenly shared.
examples.cn: 这个国家的财富分配不均。

examples.en: She has a wealth of experience in teaching children.
examples.cn: 她在儿童教育方面经验丰富。

examples.en: Health matters more than wealth.
examples.cn: 健康比财富更重要。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威尔士」——威尔士老矿主家的木箱里塞满地契和银器，那就是 wealth。

root: 古英语 wela（安康、兴旺）→ weal + 抽象词尾 -th → 中古英语 wealthe → wealth；同源词有 healthy 式的 health、welfare。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as well-being, turns into the goods that secure it, then into any abundance at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从安康出发，转为保障安康的财物，再扩展为任何充裕之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chest packed with coins and deeds.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只塞满钱币与地契的箱子。

branches.en: The economic branch: money, land and the condition of having them.
branches.cn: 经济分支：钱财、土地，以及拥有它们的状态。

branches.en: The abundance branch: a wealth of evidence.
branches.cn: 充裕分支：大量证据。

branches.en: The resource branch: teachers as a nation’s wealth.
branches.cn: 资源分支：人才作为国家的财富。

branches.en: The old branch: the wealth of a whole town as its good.
branches.cn: 旧义分支：全镇的福祉。

branches.en: The origin branch: weal, the well-being that started it.
branches.cn: 起源分支：起始处的安康，即 weal。

intro.en: Wealth is a native abstract noun, so its affixes are the old -th ending and the modern -y adjective ending.
intro.cn: wealth 是本土抽象名词，其构词就是古老的 -th 词尾与现代 -y 形容词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic, so the Latin table is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语，故拉丁表留空。

items.example: It is the root of the family.

items.exampleCN: 它把 weal 变成 wealth。

definition_zh: 富有的；富裕的；丰富的
definition_en: having a large amount of money and possessions, or having plenty of something valuable
core_image: 一间储满粮食与布匹的库房，门一开就能看出屋主的家底
scene: 村口的宅子有石墙和两层楼，院子里停着两辆车。The town grew wealthy on the wool trade in the sixteenth century.
sceneCN: 这里 wealthy 是「富有的」（第 1 个义项：拥有大量钱财与产业）；句意为这座城镇在十六世纪靠羊毛贸易富了起来。库房里堆满的粮食与布匹，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 形容词：富有的；富裕的；丰富的、大量的

derivatives.zh: 本词的词根名词，义为「财富；大量」
加副词后缀构成，义为「富足地；阔气地」
加名词后缀构成，义为「富裕」
与 well 相关的形近词，义为「福祉；幸福」

senses.title: Having much money
senses.titleCN: 富有的：拥有大量钱财与产业
senses.definition: having a great deal of money, property or other material goods
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大量金钱、产业或其他物质财富
senses.example: The wealthy merchant owned four ships and half the dock.
senses.exampleCN: 这位富商拥有四条船和半个码头。
senses.why: Old English weal means well-being, and wealth was originally that whole state; money became its measure.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 weal 意为「安好」，wealth 本指整个好境况；金钱后来成了它的度量。

senses.title: As a group
senses.titleCN: 富人：作为一个群体来看的富有者
senses.definition: in the phrase the wealthy, the whole group of rich people
senses.definitionCN: 用于 the wealthy，指全部富人这一群体
senses.example: The tax falls hardest on the wealthy and lightest on the poor.
senses.exampleCN: 这项税对富人最重，对穷人最轻。
senses.why: Adjectives preceded by the can name a class, so the rich quality turns into the people who have it.
senses.whyCN: 形容词前加 the 可以指一类人，于是「富」这一性质变成了拥有它的人群。

senses.title: Rich in natural goods
senses.titleCN: 资源丰富的：物产或条件富足
senses.definition: rich in natural resources, land or production
senses.definitionCN: 在自然资源、土地或产出方面富足
senses.example: The valley is wealthy in water, which the plains below lack.
senses.exampleCN: 这条山谷水源丰富，而下面的平原却缺水。
senses.why: The abundance that money measures also exists in land: the word follows the goods, not the bank account.
senses.whyCN: 金钱所衡量的那种充足也存在于土地中：这个词跟的是物产，而不是银行户头。

senses.title: Rich in a quality
senses.titleCN: 丰富的：在某种特质上含量多
senses.definition: having a large amount of a particular quality or element, used figuratively
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指某种品质或成分含量很多
senses.example: The region is wealthy in stories, and every village tells them differently.
senses.exampleCN: 这一带故事极多，每个村庄讲得都不一样。
senses.why: Once plenty is the meaning, anything countable can be the treasure that fills the storehouse.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「充足」成了核心义，任何可数的东西都能成为填满库房的宝藏。

senses.title: Prosperous in life
senses.definition: enjoying a comfortable and prosperous way of life, without the stress on huge sums
senses.definitionCN: 生活舒适宽裕，不特别强调数目巨大
senses.example: After two good harvests the farmhouse looked wealthy again.
senses.exampleCN: 连收两季好庄稼之后，那座农舍又显得富足了。
senses.why: This is the old well-being again, visible in a house rather than counted in coins.
senses.whyCN: 这又回到了古老的「安好」，它显在一座房子里，而不是数在铜板中。

intro.en: Wealthy grows from wealth, whose oldest sense was not money but well-being.
intro.cn: wealthy 由 wealth 生长而来，而 wealth 最初的意思不是钱，而是「安好」。

items.en: Weal meant 'well-being, welfare, prosperity', the same element as in commonweal.
items.cn: weal 意为「安好、福祉、兴旺」，与 commonweal 中的成分相同。

items.en: Wela meant 'wealth, riches', and the two words were closely associated.
items.cn: wela 意为「财富、财宝」，两者关系密切。

items.en: Wele or welthe came to name both prosperity and the things that show it.
items.cn: 中古英语 wele 与 welthe 既指兴旺，也指显出兴旺的那些东西。

items.en: The suffix -y forms the adjective, and wealthy appears alongside the older wele. Exact first dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 后缀 -y 构成形容词 wealthy，它与更早的 wele 并存；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The sense narrowed toward money and property, while the figurative sense of abundance survived.
items.cn: 词义向金钱与财产收窄，而表示「丰富」的比喻义照旧留存。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the wealth family; the near-meaning group gathers words for being rich.
note.cn: 形近组收 wealth 一族词；近义组收表示富有的词。

entries.definition: Riches, or a large amount of something good.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「财富」，或指某物的「大量」。

entries.definition: The abstract noun for the state of being wealthy; rare in speech.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「富裕」，口语中罕见。

entries.definition: The state of being well in body; a shared shape, different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「健康」，与 wealthy 形近而义不同。

entries.definition: A political community; keeps the old weal of well-being.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「联邦、共同体」，保留了 weal「福祉」的旧义。

entries.definition: Having much money or many resources; the commonest word.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富的」，是最常用的说法。

entries.definition: Prosperous and well-off; formal and often about societies.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「富裕的」，语气正式，多用于社会群体。

entries.definition: Comfortably provided for, without implying great riches.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「宽裕的」，不含巨富之意。

entries.definition: Thriving and successful, often of a business or a town.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「兴旺的」，多形容事业或城镇。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English weal and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语 weal，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: wealth began as well-being, and only later counted money.
normal.cn: wealth 起初指安好，后来才开始数钱。

normal.en: Wealthy adds -y to wealth, just as healthy adds -y to health.
normal.cn: wealthy 由 wealth 加 -y，正如 healthy 由 health 加 -y。

normal.en: The wealthy means all rich people together, not one rich person.
normal.cn: the wealthy 指全部富人，不是某一位富人。

normal.en: A region can be wealthy in water or in stories, not only in cash.
normal.cn: 一个地区可以水富、故事富，不只是钱富。

normal.en: Well-off is milder than wealthy; it stops short of great riches.
normal.cn: well-off 比 wealthy 温和，不含巨富之意。

abstract.en: Picture a storehouse packed with grain and cloth: the wealth shows in what can be drawn on.
abstract.cn: 想象一间堆满粮食与布匹的库房：财富显现在可取用的东西上。

abstract.en: The word measures plenty, so it can point at money, water, or a store of tales.
abstract.cn: 这个词衡量的是「充足」，所以能指向金钱、水，或一大堆故事。

abstract.en: Its oldest layer is not greed but welfare: to be wealthy once meant to be well.
abstract.cn: 它最古老的一层不是贪婪而是福祉：有钱曾经意味着过得好。

examples.en: The wealthy family owned most of the land in the valley.
examples.cn: 那个富裕家族拥有谷中大部分土地。

examples.en: The country is wealthy in forests but poor in oil.
examples.cn: 这个国家森林丰富，却缺乏石油。

examples.en: The shop moved to a wealthier district last spring.
examples.cn: 这家店去年春天搬到了更富裕的街区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威（weal）尔西（thy）」——威尔西家库房里粮布堆到屋顶：富有的

root: 由中古英语 welthe「兴旺、财富」加形容词后缀 -y 构成，更早来自古英语 weal「福祉」与 wela「财富」；同族词有 wealth、commonwealth。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of wealthy run from cash and property to the class of rich people, then to abundance of resources, of qualities, and of a comfortable life.
sensesIntro.cn: wealthy 的五个义项从钱财产业出发，到富人这一群体，再到资源充足、品质丰富，以及生活宽裕。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a storehouse packed with grain and cloth, its wealth plain as soon as the door opens.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间堆满粮食布匹的库房，门一开就看得出家底。

branches.en: MONEY LINE: cash, property and a comfortable life.
branches.cn: 金钱线：现金、产业与宽裕的生活。

branches.en: CLASS LINE: the adjective becomes a name for rich people.
branches.cn: 群体线：形容词成了富人的称呼。

branches.en: PLENTY LINE: water, forests or stories in abundance.
branches.cn: 充足线：水、森林或故事方面的丰富。

branches.en: ROOT LINE: the old sense of well-being still glows under the money.
branches.cn: 词根线：金钱之下还隐约闪着古老的「安好」义。

branches.en: CONTRAST: rich is plainer, affluent more formal.
branches.cn: 对照线：rich 更朴素，affluent 更正式。

intro.en: Wealthy is a native noun plus the common adjective suffix -y.
intro.cn: wealthy 是本族名词加常见形容词后缀 -y 构成的。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved here; the related native forms are listed instead.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不涉及拉丁语成分，只列出相关的本族词形式。

definition_zh: 武器；兵器；手段（斗争或取胜的凭借）
definition_en: an object used to hurt or defeat an opponent, and also any method used to win a struggle
core_image: 一把长矛斜靠在石墙上，矛尖还有磨过的亮痕
scene: 博物馆的玻璃柜里，一支锈迹斑斑的长矛横放在绒布上，旁边标签写着它的出土年代。The spear in the case was the first weapon found at the site.
sceneCN: 这里 weapon 是「武器」（第 1 个义项：用来伤害或战胜对手的器具）；句意为柜中这支长矛是遗址出土的第一件武器。斜靠石墙、矛尖带亮痕的长矛就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: An object made to hurt
senses.definition: a tool or device designed to injure, kill or defeat an opponent
senses.definitionCN: 为伤害、杀死或击败对手而设计的器具
senses.example: The soldiers laid down their weapons at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵们在黎明时放下武器。
senses.why: This is the physical core: a made thing with a harmful purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理核心：一件有伤害用途的制成品。

senses.title: Armed force in general
senses.definition: armed strength seen as a whole, as in a balance of weapons
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体来看的武装力量，如武器平衡
senses.example: Talks on limiting weapons resumed last week.
senses.exampleCN: 限制军备的会谈上周恢复。
senses.why: One object becomes a class of objects and then a form of power.
senses.whyCN: 一件器物成为一类器物，再成为一种力量。

senses.title: A means of winning a struggle
senses.definition: anything used to gain an advantage in an argument, contest or campaign
senses.definitionCN: 在争论、竞争或运动中用来取得优势的任何东西
senses.example: Information is the most useful weapon in this campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 在这场竞选里，信息是最有用的武器。
senses.why: A contest is fought like a battle, so its best tool becomes a weapon.
senses.whyCN: 竞争也像打仗一样进行，于是最好的工具就成了武器。

senses.title: A way of fighting something harmful
senses.definition: a method used against a disease, a problem or a natural danger
senses.definitionCN: 用来对抗疾病、问题或自然危险的方法
senses.example: Vaccination is our best weapon against the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 疫苗是我们对抗这种疾病的最好手段。
senses.why: Even a fight against illness borrows the language of arms.
senses.whyCN: 连对抗疾病也借用了兵器的说法。

senses.title: Something one is skilled with
senses.definition: a skill or quality that gives its owner an advantage
senses.definitionCN: 给拥有者带来优势的技能或特质
senses.example: Her patience was a weapon in long negotiations.
senses.exampleCN: 在漫长的谈判中，她的耐心就是一件利器。
senses.why: A personal quality that wins ground is spoken of as if it were carried in the hand.
senses.whyCN: 能赢下一块地盘的个人品质，被说得像握在手中一样。

intro.en: Weapon comes from Old English wǣpen, a Germanic word of unknown deeper origin, and has meant an instrument of fighting for a thousand years.
intro.cn: weapon 来自古英语 wǣpen，是更早来源不明的日耳曼词，一千年来一直指打斗的器具。

items.en: The Germanic form wǣpnam named an implement of battle, and related words survive in Dutch and German.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 wǣpnam 指战斗器具，荷兰语与德语中仍有相关词。

items.en: Wǣpen could mean a single weapon or arms in general, and appeared in heroic poetry.
items.cn: wǣpen 可指单件武器，也可泛指武装，见于英雄诗歌。

items.en: Spelling shifted towards weapon, and the plural weapons became the usual collective form.
items.cn: 拼写趋向 weapon，复数 weapons 成为常用集合形式。

items.en: Gunpowder gave the word a second life in phrases such as nuclear weapons.
items.cn: 火药与核技术让这个词在 nuclear weapons 等说法中获得第二次生命。

items.en: The figurative use, a weapon against poverty, is now entirely standard.
items.cn: 比喻用法「对抗贫困的武器」如今已完全标准。

note.en: The first group is built on the weapon word itself, the second are the other names for arms.
note.cn: 第一组建立在 weapon 这个词上，第二组是武器的其他说法。

entries.definitionCN: 无武器的

entries.definitionCN: 武器；军械

entries.definitionCN: 枪；炮

entries.definitionCN: 工具

entries.definitionCN: 手段；方法

normalIntro.en: Keep the physical weapon in view, then let it travel into arguments and medicine.
normalIntro.cn: 先盯住实物武器，再看它走进争论与医学。

normal.en: Weapon is the singular; arms is the plural collective.
normal.cn: weapon 是单数，arms 是复数集合。

normal.en: Weaponry is the mass noun for weapons as a whole.
normal.cn: weaponry 作为物质名词指全部武器。

normal.en: Weaponize means to make a weapon of something.
normal.cn: weaponize 是把某物做成武器。

normal.en: A weapon against a disease is a cure, not a gun.
normal.cn: a weapon against a disease 是疗法，不是枪。

normal.en: Information as a weapon is the commonest figurative use.
normal.cn: 信息作为武器是最常见的比喻用法。

abstract.en: Picture a spear leaning on cold stone.
abstract.cn: 想一支矛斜靠在冰冷的石上。

abstract.en: Feel the balance of a long shaft in one hand.
abstract.cn: 感受一只手握长杆时的重量平衡。

abstract.en: See a sign that says the spear was the first of its kind here.
abstract.cn: 看一块牌子写着这是此地出土的第一件。

examples.en: The police found a weapon in the car.
examples.cn: 警察在车里发现了一件武器。

examples.en: Education is a powerful weapon against poverty.
examples.cn: 教育是对抗贫困的有力武器。

examples.en: They accused each other of using gossip as a weapon.
examples.cn: 他们互相指责对方把流言当武器。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威朋」——威朋把长矛靠在门口，说这是护家的第一件武器。

root: 日耳曼语 wǣpnam（战斗器具）→ 古英语 wǣpen → 中古英语 weapon；同源词有 weaponry、weaponize。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as one made object, widens to armed force, then turns to any means of winning or fighting.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一件制成品出发，扩大到武装力量，再转向任何取胜或对抗的手段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spear leaning against a stone wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支斜靠石墙的长矛。

branches.en: The object branch: weapons laid down at dawn.
branches.cn: 器物分支：黎明时放下的武器。

branches.en: The collective branch: talks on limiting weapons.
branches.cn: 集合分支：限制军备的会谈。

branches.en: The means branch: information in a campaign, a vaccine against illness.
branches.cn: 手段分支：竞选中的信息，对抗疾病的疫苗。

branches.en: The personal branch: patience as a negotiator’s weapon.
branches.cn: 个人分支：谈判者的耐心。

branches.en: The origin branch: an object held in the hand.
branches.cn: 起源分支：握在手中的器物。

intro.en: Weapon takes the ordinary noun and verb endings of English, chiefly in modern coinages.
intro.cn: weapon 采用英语常见的名词与动词词尾，主要用于现代新造词。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin source, so the Latin table stays empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁来源，故拉丁表留空。
